items.t: 1Password launches a way for AI agents to log in on your behalf without seeing your password
items.d: The new feature allows agents to log into a customer's personal accounts while still protecting the private credentials that secure those accounts.
items.x:
The new feature allows agents to log into a customer's personal accounts while still protecting the private credentials that secure those accounts.
Concerns have swirled over the access that consumers are increasingly entrusting to AI agents. Now, security services are trying to catch up.
Password manager 1Password on Thursday launched a new tool by which users can allow agents to log into their personal accounts on their behalf, without the agent ever having access to a user’s credentials.
The new platform, dubbed 1Password for Agents, accomplishes this by creating a system of communication between the agent, the user, and the password manager. When an agent attempts to log in on a user’s behalf, a unique digital key is sent to 1Password to confirm the agent’s digital identity. The user is then sent an alert about the login attempt and can personally confirm the request. 1Password then signs in the agent, filling in the credentials on the digital assistant’s behalf, which allows it to log in and complete whatever task is at hand.
1Password for Agents allows users to choose their agent of choice — whether that’s Claude Duet from Anthropic, OpenAI’s Dots or ChatGPT Work, Grok Bot, Meta’s Muse, or agents from Town, which is an AI assistant startup.

items.t: Canva releases its first image generation model
items.d: Canva is making its new image model available to all users, promising better, more customizable performance at lower costs.
items.x:
Canva is making its new image model available to all users, promising better, more customizable performance at lower costs.
Design platform Canva released its first image generation model, called Canva Craft, developed by its research team to compete with same-category models from Google, OpenAI, ByteDance, and Meta.
The company said its model works in two stages. In the first stage, it interprets users’ prompts and creates a plan with details like spatial relationships of elements, relative scale, visual hierarchy, and information for text generation. In the second stage, its model generates an image of up to 2K resolution in a possible 30 different aspect ratios for various platforms.
Canva said that this approach allows it to create images with accurate details of objects and legible text. Plus, users would be able to make precise edits without changing other parts of the image.
The company noted that rather than using photographs, it used designs to train this model using human-designed templates from Canva’s library, including posters, social posts, presentations, infographics, menus, and typography-rich layouts.
That means images generated with Canva Craft could be converted into layered designs using Canva Magic, the company’s image-to-design transformer.

items.t: OpenAI makes its Jev competitor widely available as decision model competition heats up
items.d: OpenAI is launching its decision model to the world. Can it compete with the original Jev?
items.x:
OpenAI is launching its decision model to the world. Can it compete with the original Jev?
OpenAI made its Decisions API model widely available to users for the first time, entering the market for fast, cheap intelligence that recently made TypeSafe, a startup founded by a former researcher at the frontier lab, a $7.6 billion company.
TypeSafe’s Jev model created a category for deep learning models that act as super classifiers: Given a set of options, they can quickly make choices and offer a confidence rating in their decision. Software developers quickly found that these decision or System One models could replace LLMs in a variety of workflows, operating more quickly and a at dramatically lower cost.
Nikunj Handa, the product lead for OpenAI’s APIs, told TechCrunch that his colleagues saw Jev and said “wow, we we have like a million use cases for this.” Handa’s team sprinted to offer their own version: Rather than building a specifically calibrated decision model, the team took ChatGPT Luna and reconfigured it to speed up the inference and lower the cost.
“The big unlock with Decisions API has been the speed, shrinking things from one to three seconds to 100, 120, 180 milliseconds,” Handa said.

items.t: Microsoft’s Mustafa Suleyman says its AI outperforms doctors on hard cases as he chases ‘medical superintelligence’
items.d: Microsoft’s new AI diagnostic system beat generalist doctors on hard cases, according to a study in Science. But most of the improvement seems to come from the AI models underneath, not from Microsoft’s system itself.
items.x:
Microsoft’s new AI diagnostic system beat generalist doctors on hard cases, according to a study in Science. But most of the improvement seems to come from the AI models underneath, not from Microsoft’s system itself.
Microsoft’s AI diagnostic system correctly diagnosed complex medical cases in a simulation more than twice as often as generalist physicians, according to a study published Thursday in Science. Mustafa Suleyman, Microsoft AI’s CEO, called the result a step toward “medical superintelligence.”
The system, dubbed MAI-DxO (DxO for short), coordinates several AI agents that act like a panel of doctors. They question a patient, order tests, and debate a diagnosis.
In a simulation using complex cases from the New England Journal of Medicine, it was correct 83% of the time. Primary care doctors and general internists, working individually with reference materials, were correct 36% of the time. One note: cases this complex are usually handled by specialists or physician teams, who weren’t part of the comparison.
“There is something very substantial and exciting here,” Dominic King, vice president of Health at Microsoft AI, told TechCrunch.

items.t: Chinese hackers spied on thousands of companies after breaching IT giant ConnectWise
items.d: Microsoft points the blame for ConnectWise's breach at a China-aligned hacker, which relied on AI agents to rapidly hack into thousands of its customers.
items.x:
Microsoft points the blame for ConnectWise's breach at a China-aligned hacker, which relied on AI agents to rapidly hack into thousands of its customers.
The bad week for cybersecurity just got worse for thousands more companies, who were spied on by Chinese hackers following the breach of IT management and remote access giant ConnectWise.
Security researchers at Microsoft say the China state-aligned hackers broke into ConnectWise’s cloud backup service and stole application credentials that are used to establish data links between ConnectWise and its corporate customers, who rely on the cloud service to backup their company’s data.
By stealing the credentials, the hackers could log in to the customer’s Microsoft-hosted environment as if they were an authorized user and access their emails and other files.
According to Microsoft, the hackers used AI agents to rapidly hack into around 2,250 organizations at a rate of almost 3,000 attempted sign-ins per minute. Microsoft said this speed gives defenders “little time to detect and respond.”
The speed of the mass-hacks were attributed to the use of AI agents, specifically ARTEX, an open-source AI framework that works with AI models to stress-test cyber defenses.

items.t: PHP: The three little letters wreaking havoc across the web
items.d: Two vulnerabilities found in the programming language PHP put enormous swaths of the internet in danger. By some accounts, up to 70 percent of websites use PHP in some capacity. It powers Wikipedia, WordPress, Drupal, and a host of other…
items.x:
Two vulnerabilities found in the programming language PHP put enormous swaths of the internet in danger .
By some accounts, up to 70 percent of websites use PHP in some capacity. It powers Wikipedia, WordPress, Drupal, and a host of other popular sites and platforms, including DeviantArt and 4Chan, which were temporarily shut down after the vulnerabilities were disclosed. Even governments weren’t immune.
But it’s not as simple as updating a few servers. The vulnerability exists in every version of PHP dating back roughly 20 years, many of which are no longer supported. That means some older sites and services that are no longer actively maintained are at risk, leaving them with little option but to permanently shut down.
Here’s all the latest developments in what security firm Wiz has called “among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered … in software history.”
Two old-school Japanese mobile games are shutting down over the PHP exploit.
The PHP2Shell exploit hit Cloudflare hard.

items.t: OlmoEarth v1.3: State-of-the-art embeddings for the whole planet
items.x:
🤗 Models | 📄 Tech Report | 📊 Data | 💻 Code | 🌎 Embeddings Explorer | 🗺️ Interactive story
Today, we’re releasing OlmoEarth v1.3, a state-of-the-art satellite embedding model. Alongside OlmoEarth v1.3, we’re sharing precomputed, annual embeddings for the whole planet (10m, 64- and 128-dimensions), plus a new browser-based tool to explore and customize maps based on those embeddings — the OlmoEarth Embeddings Explorer. This means anyone can put OlmoEarth v1.3 to work right away, from tracking change over time to finding similar places—no sign-in, and no advanced technical knowledge required.
Until now, the primary way to use OlmoEarth was fine-tuning in OlmoEarth Studio: training a model for each task and running it over satellite imagery to make a map. That requires GPU access and the ability to download and store the imagery. Embedding models compress satellite data into ready-to-use features that can be reused cheaply for many tasks.
With OlmoEarth v1.3, we’re excited to give users more ways to explore and engage with planetary artifacts in whatever way suits them best.
An embedding represents what the model learned from millions of images.

items.t: Uber puts all 30,000 employees on ChatGPT Work
items.d: The ride-share giant previously deployed a much smaller pilot for ChatGPT Work but is now taking the enterprise agent company-wide.
items.x:
The ride share giant previously deployed a much smaller pilot for ChatGPT Work, but is now taking the enterprise agent company-wide.
Uber and OpenAI announced an expansion of their partnership on Thursday, with the ride-share giant telling TechCrunch that its entire global workforce — some 30,000 people — will now be using ChatGPT Work.
ChatGPT Work was introduced in July as an enterprise-focused AI agent that corporate teams could deploy for various workflows.
Uber originally piloted ChatGPT Work with 1,000 employees earlier this year but has now scaled up its usage to the entire company.
That earlier pilot was deployed to workers from across Uber’s various departments, including finance, operations, and product. Indeed, a majority of the early adopters — some 80% — were non-engineers, Sumanth Sukumar, Uber’s VP of engineering, told TechCrunch.
“They used it for a wide range of tasks: analyzing complex data from our operations to identify trends and develop recommendations; localizing training materials for different markets and languages; and building personalized interactive dashboards to manage their daily work,” he said.
Yet while the ride-share giant is now going all-in on ChatGPT, it sounds not to have settled on exactly how employees will use it.

items.t: Spotify’s current AI bet is about being the music service that agents choose
items.d: Spotify co-CEO Gustav Söderström explains why the rise of AI agents could be good news for the music service.
items.x:
Spotify co-CEO Gustav Söderström explains why the rise of AI agents could be good news for the music service.
Spotify had a strong third quarter, reaching 788 million monthly active users and generating nearly €5 billion (around $5.6 billion USD) in revenue. But the more interesting takeaway from its earnings call was how the company sees people listening to music in the future, and why the rise of AI agents could be good news for its business.
Co-CEO Gustav Söderström thinks the music streaming giant is particularly well suited to this shift.
“Spotify is in one of the few categories that actually stands to thrive in the agentic age,” Söderström tells investors. “This is because agents excel at replacing and taking care of things people would rather not do. People love getting rid of chores. But entertainment is the opposite. Nobody asks an agent to ‘summarize a song’ for them.”
Instead of opening Spotify, searching for an artist and building a playlist themselves, listeners could ask an AI assistant to do the work for them.

items.x:
Launched today, NVIDIA Minerva is an AIOps platform built to help teams find problems earlier and keep AI factories productive. It brings together telemetry from infrastructure and AI workloads, then applies purpose-built AI models to turn that data into timely, actionable insight.
AI factories are among the most complex operations in the world, with vast numbers of GPUs working across high-speed networks to train models and serve AI applications. At that scale, a single degraded component can slow an entire job. The warning signs may be easy to miss, such as a GPU running hotter than its peers or an NVMe drive losing performance under load.
The platform focuses on AI factory yield, a measure of the useful work infrastructure produces through GPU hours, goodput, cluster uptime and token production.
Delivering a Dynamic View of an AI Factory
Traditional monitoring tools often divide the data center into separate views. Networking, compute, site reliability and machine learning teams each see a different part of the operation.

items.t: Beyond tree cover: mapping the world’s forest types
items.d: A global map categorizing every 10-meter patch of land on Earth into distinct forest types.
items.x:
Explore Forest Typology (ForTy) 2020: a global 10-meter map categorizing Earth's land into six distinct forest and land-use types, plus an annual time series.
A new 10-meter resolution map shows which of the world's forests are natural, planted, or farmed, and how they are changing over time
Protecting the planet's forests starts with a simple question: what type of forest are we looking at? From space, an old-growth rainforest, a eucalyptus plantation, and an oil palm estate can look like the same patch of green. But they hold very different amounts of carbon and biodiversity. Telling them apart, and knowing how each patch has changed over time, shows us where conservation is working and where natural forests are being converted into plantations and farms.
Today, Google DeepMind and Google Research, together with the World Resources Institute (WRI) and the International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis (IIASA), are releasing Forest Typology (ForTy) 2020, a global map that categorizes every 10-by-10-meter patch of land on Earth into six distinct forest and land-use types, a key baseline for the EU's deforestation regulation.

The AI world is flooded with personal and productivity-based assistants, with new ones launching every week. Now, Anthropic is entering this battle in the hopes of gaining user attention with a new app called Claude Duet, aimed at rivaling Meta Muse, OpenAI Dots, Hark, Instinct, Grok Bot, and Fo.
Anthropic said the new agent is meant to cater to professionals and small businesses to help them with automating and managing tasks. The company is making a distinction from personal agents such as Instinct, by noting that Duet isn’t good at handling errands or booking tickets, and it can’t show you its browser use as it happens.
Instead, Duet can build a daily briefing for its users, create dashboards, or suggest actions based on the user’s data. Like other agents, Duet can complete tasks in the background through its own virtual machine while you handle other things, then come back to you if it needs your approval.
The launch arrives as the market shifts beyond AI assistants to agents that can work on users’ behalf. Many of Anthropic’s rivals are focusing on business use cases.

Nirva will ship its $249 ambient AI pendant by the end of the year.
Ambient AI is having a moment. Amazon launched a new wrist-worn device with Bee; a former Plaud exec launched ambient apps through a startup called Ambi, which aims to also build its own hardware; and Apple launched Voice Intelligence features during its iPhone launch in September. Now, a company called Nirva is betting on a jewelry-like pendant and its ability to listen only to the wearer.
The startup today announced a new $25 million pre-Series A round, adding to the $8 million it raised earlier in the year from investors like Lightspeed and South Park Commons, bringing its total raise to $33 million.
Nirva was founded in 2025 by two former Meta Reality Labs employees, Wei Lyu and Jason Chen, along with Hanying Hu, who founded a fashion and jewelry brand.

items.t: Bill Gates says to prepare for 20 years of ‘tumultuous’ AI disruption
items.d: Today, I’m talking to Bill Gates, cofounder and former CEO of Microsoft and chairman of the Gates Foundation. You may have noticed Bill in the news more lately — he’s been on something of a tour for the past few months, ever since…

Nicky Quamina-Woo " data-has-syndication-rights="1" src="https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/268806_Bill_Gates_NQuamina-Woo_0007_a8ca1f.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100" />
Today, I’m talking to Bill Gates, cofounder and former CEO of Microsoft and chairman of the Gates Foundation.
You may have noticed Bill in the news more lately — he’s been on something of a tour for the past few months, ever since publishing an essay in late August titled “The turbulent AI era is here. The choices we make now are critical.”
In his piece, Gates ratcheted up his rhetoric around AI safety, writing that “even under the best circumstances, the transition to this new AI era will be one of the most turbulent times in human history.”
In interviews since , Gates has called AI “the most dangerous thing that humans have ever gone near,” and that AI “makes nuclear weapons look like nothing.” It is clear he does not think the current policy response from the White House, or the lack of coordinated efforts from the AI industry itself, is sufficient to combat this threat.
So I wanted to know: Is Bill Gates an AI doomer? I also had a series of questions downstream from what he’s been arguing about AI.

items.t: Making the case for context-aware AI
items.d: Enterprise AI can generate recommendations, automate tasks, and help organizations make decisions faster. But without an understanding of how a business actually operates, even powerful models can miss the constraints and relationships…
items.x:
Enterprise AI can generate recommendations, automate tasks, and help organizations make decisions faster. But without an understanding of how a business actually operates, even powerful models can miss the constraints and relationships that determine whether a decision is the right one. As companies look to move AI from experimentation into everyday operations, the challenge ahead is giving technology the context to act usefully within complex business processes.
For Devavrat Shah, chief scientist of enterprise AI at Celonis, that context is central to what he calls “decision intelligence.” AI agents can support individual tasks within larger decision-making processes, he argues, but they need to understand the role each task plays and the business conditions surrounding it. “You can’t just do that in a vacuum,” he says. Without the right operational context, agents risk overlooking important constraints, making costly mistakes, or consuming excessive computing resources as they try to work out what they need to know.
The solution begins with connecting AI to the processes and data enterprises already use. A contextual layer can help agents understand workflows, operate within defined guardrails, and produce recommendations that people can review and approve.

items.t: AI’s hidden storage bill: What inference leaves behind
items.d: Ask most executives to picture the cost of AI and they’ll likely see GPUs—racks of accelerators with gigawatts of power—and a waitlist for silicon. But that picture leaves something out: Data storage costs. What happens to data after a…
items.x:
Ask most executives to picture the cost of AI and they’ll likely see GPUs—racks of accelerators with gigawatts of power—and a waitlist for silicon. But that picture leaves something out: Data storage costs.
What happens to data after a model responds? Much of the back-end data that’s generated—from billions of daily prompts, images, and videos—needs to be stored. But data storage is one of the harder infrastructure costs to plan for, and it’s often overlooked in initial AI infrastructure planning.
As inference scales, the data footprint grows with it
Traditionally, AI infrastructure conversations have centered on the compute-intensive process of training a model. Training is finite: a run starts, burns through compute, and ends. But inference runs continuously, every time a model answers a prompt. For infrastructure planning, that difference matters: A training run is a project you can budget for and retire. Inference doesn’t retire; every inference request leaves something behind.
Take AI-generated video. In this workload, the back-end spend can be significant.

items.t: Ensemble forecasting with IBM Granite time-series models
items.x:
Four open Granite models, one extensible forecasting interface, and less guesswork about which model to use.
Pre-trained time-series models can forecast without training on your dataset, but you still have to choose one. A model that handles smooth industrial signals well may struggle with noisy retail demand or a long seasonal horizon, and the best choice depends on the series and the task.
Granite Timeseries Ensemble reduces that choice to a sensible default. One recipe combines four complementary Granite architectures and returns median and quantile forecasts, with no retraining and no fitted ensemble weights. Start with the Probabilistic Ensemble (uniform probability pooling), compare the adaptive Inter Quartile Range (IQR) Ensemble, and extend the same interface with compatible forecasters. The ensemble recipe and its default Granite members are permissively licensed.
The idea will be familiar from weather forecasting. Ensemble forecasts explore a range of possible outcomes, and systems such as the North American Multi-Model Ensemble combine different models for seasonal prediction.

items.t: Tsinghua AIR Spinout Tairex Brings Multi-Specialty AI Doctor Avatars Into Outpatient Clinics
items.d: Tairex, incubated by Tsinghua AIR, launched MHAC, a framework that lets a clinic doctor call in AI avatars of other specialists for advice, while human doctors keep the final decision.
items.x:
Tairex, an AI healthcare company incubated by Tsinghua University's Institute for AI Industry Research (AIR), has launched a framework it calls Multidisciplinary Human-Agent Collaboration, or MHAC, and upgraded its Agent Hospital system. The company presented it at an event at the China National Convention Center in Beijing on October 21.
Agent Hospital itself is not new. Its research origins lie with AIR professor Liu Yang's team, which built a simulated hospital where AI doctor agents treat millions of synthetic patients, reflect on failures and distill reusable rules. What is new is the step from single AI assistants to coordinated avatars of different specialists working inside ordinary outpatient visits.
The target is the multidisciplinary team consultation, in which experts from several departments review one complex case. Tairex argues such consultations come late, after patients have visited several departments, are limited to large hospitals and offline meetings, and are expensive to convene. MHAC tries to bring that input into routine clinics.
In practice, a doctor sees patients as usual. As new information arrives, the system detects when another specialty is relevant and shows that specialist avatar's advice as a prompt.

items.t: BIGAI Spinout Tongyan Lingzhi Bets on Personal LoRA and Self-Improving AI Models
items.d: Tongyan Lingzhi, incubated by the Beijing Institute for General Artificial Intelligence, is building personal AI that stores user and team skills in lightweight LoRA weights updated over time.
items.x:
Tongyan Lingzhi, a company incubated by the industry platform of the Beijing Institute for General Artificial Intelligence (BIGAI), has laid out its approach to what it calls personal AI: models that keep learning from a specific person, project or company instead of relying only on prompts and retrieval.
Most enterprise AI today adapts to users from the outside. Prompts set rules, retrieval pulls in documents, memory stores state and skills package reusable steps, but the model's own weights rarely change after an interaction. Tongyan Lingzhi argues that stable habits, such as a team's engineering conventions or an investment group's risk discipline, could instead be trained into parameters.
Its architecture keeps a shared base model for general knowledge and reasoning, and adds lightweight Personal LoRA adapters for each individual, project or organization. The company says the aim is for these personal capabilities to survive when the underlying base model is swapped.
To keep those adapters learning, the team is developing recursive self-improvement, or RSI. Task traces, human corrections and outcomes become candidate training data. An evaluator, tuned to each user's or company's standards, filters which signals are worth learning from before an incremental LoRA update.

items.t: BAAI's FlagOS 2.2 Expands Its Cross-Chip Operator Libraries to 1,454 Operators
items.d: FlagOS 2.2 from the Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence grows its nine operator libraries to 1,454 operators and reports about 27% faster operators across 10 kinds of AI chips.
items.x:
The Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence (BAAI) has detailed FlagOS 2.2, the latest version of its open software stack for running AI models across different chip architectures. The release shipped on September 30 and was showcased at the 2026 AI Open Computing Conference in Beijing on October 17. BAAI describes the update as a shift from adapting models to many chips toward optimizing shared code across them.
The headline figure is scale. FlagOS 2.2 spans nine operator libraries, and public operators in FlagGems and related libraries grew from 564 to 1,454, an increase of 890. A new FlagGems-SGLang library adds 40 multi-chip operators covering attention, Mamba state updates, mixture-of-experts, LoRA, sampling and quantization. BAAI says that across more than a thousand operators on 10 kinds of AI hardware, overall operator performance rose by about 27%.
Much of the growth comes from automation. KernelGen, BAAI's automatic operator generator, now supports nine AI chips and produced 765 new operators this quarter, 416 of which passed accuracy checks on at least five domestic chips while reaching over 80% of native operator performance.

items.t: From AI generation to final cut, Fotor Agent takes on the video production workflow
items.d: If you have used AI video tools, you may have noticed an interesting trend: generating a visually impressive video is becoming easier, but turning it into a commercial-ready production is still far from simple. What happens when a subtitle…
items.x:
If you have used AI video tools, you may have noticed an interesting trend: generating a visually impressive video is becoming easier, but turning it into a commercial-ready production is still far from simple. What happens when a subtitle is wrong? What if product data needs to be updated? If a brand logo appears in the wrong place, does the entire video have to be generated again?
These issues may be acceptable for creative content on social media. But for product explainers, brand marketing and commercial advertising, videos need to be more than visually appealing. They must be accurate, visually consistent and easy to revise.
This is where Fotor Agent comes in. Launched in August, the tool builds on Fotor’s background in photo editing and visual design, extending its AI capabilities to the entire video production workflow. Rather than simply generating clips, it aims to help users turn text prompts into finished videos, from content planning to final delivery.
Users start by describing the video they want through text prompts. Fotor Agent then helps organize the production process, bringing together visual assets, subtitles, audio and animations in a single project.

items.t: How Companies Are Using NVIDIA DSX to Break the Power Bottleneck
items.d: Companies around the world are building on the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform to plan, simulate and run the grid and the AI factory as one system, from the substation to the rack. Their adoption of the platform responds to an acute…
items.x:
Companies around the world are building on the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform to plan, simulate and run the grid and the AI factory as one system, from the substation to the rack. Their adoption of the platform responds to an acute problem.
Power is now the biggest bottleneck in infrastructure. More than $300 billion in equipment is backlogged, and over 200 gigawatts of projects are waiting in U.S. interconnection queues.
One root cause of the bottleneck is siloed systems. The grid, the facility and the compute inside have long been designed independently from one another, creating the conditions for delays, risk and stranded capacity.
To help address this, NVIDIA DSX brings these systems together:
NVIDIA DSX Sim and SimReady assets from leading energy manufacturers let engineers simulate the grid, substation and AI factory together, validating generators, switchgear, power systems and cooling before breaking ground.
NVIDIA DSX Flex syncs AI factory demand with grid conditions and onsite generation, turning AI factories from static loads into flexible grid assets.
NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS and DSX Exchange squeeze more compute from every watt and securely share signals across compute, networking, energy, cooling and operations.

items.t: NVIDIA Transforms European Retail, From Digital Discovery to Physical Operations
items.d: European retailers are using open models and physical intelligence across use cases — from a commerce platform cutting inference costs by 90% to to a fulfillment center where collaboration of different robotic fleets is simulated inside a…
items.x:
European retailers are using open models and physical intelligence across use cases — from a commerce platform cutting inference costs by 90% to to a fulfillment center where collaboration of different robotic fleets is simulated inside a digital twin.
Retail leaders and technology companies across Europe are using NVIDIA-accelerated open and frontier models to advance agentic commerce, digital product discovery and retail R&D.
Shopify post-trains open models to reach frontier-level accuracy at a fraction of the cost. Its engineers use the NVIDIA Megatron Bridge library for faster fine-tuning and NVIDIA NeMo RL for reinforcement learning. Shopify has post-trained NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning for the GraphQL subagent integrated into Sidekick, Shopify’s AI assistant for merchants. The subagent retrieves store data for several Sidekick features, including Sidekick Pulse, which researches a merchant’s store and recommends ways to improve it.
On Shopify’s internal benchmark, the post-trained model surpasses a leading frontier model in accuracy while cutting serving costs by 90% and delivering responses 7x faster.

items.t: MemTensor Open-Sources MemT 1.0, Memory-Native Models That Keep Long Histories in a Fixed State
items.d: MemTensor released MemT 1.0 Flash and Nano, models with a built-in trainable memory state. It reports about 4x faster inference at 256K history and 130x smaller storage.
items.x:
Chinese AI company MemTensor has released and open-sourced MemT 1.0, a family of what it calls memory-native foundation models. The series includes two models: MemT-1.0-Flash, with 288 billion total parameters and 17 billion active, and MemT-1.0-Nano, with 36 billion total and 3 billion active. Weights are on Hugging Face and code is on GitHub alongside a technical report.
The models target a familiar cost problem in long conversations. Most systems carry the full history in the context window, so every additional turn makes inference slower and more expensive. MemT instead adds a trainable memory module inside the model. After each interaction, the model writes new information into a fixed-size memory state and recalls it when needed, rather than rereading the full record each time.
MemTensor says the models were trained in two stages on 34 billion tokens: first learning to write information into memory, then learning to answer questions from it.
All performance figures come from the company's own evaluation. MemTensor says end-to-end inference is about 1.86 times faster than a full-context approach at 128K tokens of history and about 3.99 times faster at 256K.

items.t: Lanxin Computing Unveils RISC-V Supernode Built on Its 48-Core LX500 Inference Chip
items.d: Lanxin Computing has launched a supernode built on LX500, a 48-core RISC-V chip with a 75 TOPS INT8 AI engine that puts general computing and inference on one die.
items.x:
Shenzhen-based chip designer Lanxin Computing has launched what it calls a converged-computing supernode, extending its RISC-V AI inference platform from a single chip and server to a cluster-level system. The company presented the product at the 2026 RISC-V China Summit, where chief technology officer Jia Xinxia gave a keynote on the LX500 processor that underpins it.
The idea behind the design is to cut down on data movement. In a conventional inference server, a CPU and a separate accelerator card each have their own memory, and model weights, activations and context data shuttle between them over PCIe. Lanxin's approach integrates general-purpose computing and AI computing on the same chip and lets both share a unified memory pool, which the company says helps with time to first token, prefill and long-context workloads.
According to the company, LX500 packs 48 RISC-V CPU cores, split into 32 performance cores and 16 efficiency cores, alongside AI vector and matrix engines rated at 75 TOPS of INT8 compute. It supports precisions from INT4 to FP32, shares DDR5 memory across the chip, and supports CXL memory expansion.

items.t: Donating Agent Skills to the Agentic AI Foundation
items.d: We’re donating Agent Skills, the open standard that gives AI agents specialized knowledge and workflows, to the Agentic AI Foundation. More than 70 agent platforms, including ChatGPT, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and VS Code, have integrated…
items.x:
Anthropic is an AI safety and research company that's working to build reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems.
Today, we’re donating Agent Skills, the open standard that gives AI agents specialized knowledge and workflows, to the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF). More than 70 agent platforms, including ChatGPT, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and VS Code, have integrated Agent Skills since we published the standard in December 2025.
A skill is a folder containing a SKILL.md file that teaches an agent a specific task or domain, along with any scripts or reference material it needs. We developed skills while working on Claude Code. It handled general knowledge work well, but often lacked the procedural knowledge that real business tasks need. Within weeks of our October 2025 launch, developers published thousands of skills on GitHub and wrote loaders for Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode. We then published Agent Skills as an open standard, under its own GitHub organization and domain, so any agent could use it. So far, 1 million skills have been published and nearly 280 million installed.
We’re committed to keeping Agent Skills open, community-driven, and vendor-neutral.

items.t: Building agents: When to fold subagents into your main agent loop
items.d: When building agents in Claude Platform, using fewer subagents in favor of progressively disclosed context and tools can improve quality while reducing cost and latency. Here’s when and how to migrate.
items.x:
When to consider using fewer subagents and how to migrate the into your main loop.
When building agents in Claude Platform, using fewer subagents in favor of progressively disclosed context and tools can improve quality while reducing cost and latency. Here’s when and how to migrate.
If you’ve built an agent in Claude Platform that includes multiple subagents, see which may make sense to fold into the main agent loop using our migration kit. It runs a guided workflow to identify your patterns, evaluate alternatives, and verify the best approach. It includes a demo that you can try on a mock system before running on your agent.
Subagents – agents with their own context window, tools, and instructions, orchestrated by a coordinator – are a core component of agent design. They are effective at verification, parallel work, and modular permissioning. We use them in many of our own agents that we build using Claude Platform, for example our multi-agent research system.
However, recently the Applied AI team has found a pattern of enterprise agent deployments that have benefited from folding routers, planners, and domain subagents into the main agent loop.

items.t: Blackstone’s Jas Khaira says fears over AI-buildout debt are overblown
items.d: Blackstone’s AI head on why the PE giant isn't panicked by market jitters.
items.x:
Blackstone’s AI head on why the PE giant isn't panicked by market jitters.
Private equity giant Blackstone is putting itself at the center of the AI boom, firm veteran Jas Khaira discussed last week on stage at TechCrunch Disrupt.
It is writing checks via various strategies, ranging from offering massive loans to data centers to investing in frontier AI models and applications.
Earlier this year, the firm launched Blackstone N1 (BXN1), a San Francisco-based central hub for its AI initiatives. The group is led by Khaira, who relocated from New York to be at the epicenter of AI.
Unlike earlier tech cycles such as mobile or SaaS, which allowed companies to reach significant scale with moderate capital, the transition to AI requires staggering amounts of investment. That need for capital is precisely why Blackstone, with its $1.3 trillion in assets under management, could play such a critical role in this tech shift.
Khaira emphasized that Blackstone sets itself apart from traditional venture capitalists through its focus on compute financing and its ability to offer flexible capital structures, ranging from debt to equity.

items.t: Meta wants to pay for its broad AI buildout with a newly created class of stock
items.d: The social media giant is planning a new stock strategy to help power its broad investments in AI models and services.
items.x:
The social media giant is planning a new stock strategy to help power its broad investments in AI models and services.
Meta is making a big push into AI, and it’s creating a new kind of stock that could help pay for it.
On Wednesday, as the company reported its third-quarter earnings, Semafor reported the company might issue non-voting stock, meaning shares that don’t give their owners a vote on company decisions, to help fund its push into artificial intelligence.
During Meta’s earnings call, the company confirmed that reporting. Meta’s chief financial officer, Susan Li, said the company plans to “create a new class of non-voting capital stock, which will be distributed to all existing shareholders through a stock dividend.”
Li later added that the company “created this new class of shares with the purpose of creating a publicly traded non-voting stock usable for capital raising, employee compensation, acquisitions, and other general corporate purposes while preserving the voting power of existing Class A and B shareholders.”
The shares will allow the company to maintain its current “founder-led structure,” she added.

items.t: Meta says Muse has over 10M users, with shopping a top activity
items.d: Meta Muse users are adopting the app for shopping and personal productivity, the company said during its Q3 earnings call. The AI app now has over 10M users.
items.x:
Meta Muse users are adopting the app for shopping and personal productivity, the company said during Q3 earnings. The AI app now has over 10M users.
Meta said during its third-quarter earnings call on Wednesday that its AI app Muse has been adopted by more than 10 million users, confirming estimates released earlier this week by market intelligence firm Sensor Tower.
But it is how people are using it, and how much they’re spending that has caught CEO Mark Zuckerberg’s attention. Zuckerberg said about 25% of people who set up Muse now use it daily, helping improve retention.
He also shared that over a quarter of Muse’s engaged users who were shopping via the AI agent, had an average purchase size of over $200, which was surprising even to industry insiders.
“Plaid told us that they hadn’t seen activity like they’re seeing with their connector on any other service before,” Zuckerberg said, referring to the financial technology company that connects payment apps to customers’ bank accounts. Muse uses Plaid’s connector to enable agentic shopping.
Beyond shopping, Zuckerberg said other popular uses for Muse include personal productivity tasks, such as connecting the AI agent to users’ email or calendars.

items.t: Recursive launches Flint, a laptop coding model it says was largely built by AI
items.d: Startup Recursive has released Flint, a free, laptop-sized coding model built largely by its own AI research system, as an early test of AI that improves itself.
items.x:
Startup Recursive has released Flint, a free, laptop-sized coding model built largely by its own AI research system, as an early test of AI that improves itself.
Recursive, an AI startup founded last year, is starting to live up to its name. The company, which is trying to build AI that can improve itself, released its first model, Flint, on Wednesday. Flint is a free coding model that can run on a laptop and was built largely with the help of AI.
Recursive’s automated research system, which it calls the Eureka Machine, helped with nearly every step of Flint’s development, the company says. That let a small team build the model from scratch in under four months.
Flint is an early public test of recursive self-improvement: the idea that AI can build better AI, which in turn builds even better AI. It’s also one of the most debated ideas in the industry. Some researchers fear that AI improving itself could slip out of human control. For now, Recursive’s version is more limited: an AI research assistant overseen by people that produced a model small enough for a laptop.
The company emerged from stealth in May with $650 million in funding at a $4.65 billion valuation, from backers including GV, Nvidia, and AMD Ventures.

items.t: The new human-crafted Apple Music brand matters in an AI world
items.d: Opinion: In a world of AI slop, showing the human hands making things helps.
items.x:
Apple just revealed a new brand identity for Apple Music, with the expected turn to Liquid Glass. I’m not much of a fan of their new design language in general; this is where I admit that I’m still running MacOS Sequoia and have grumpy things to say about rounded corner radii and text legibility.
It’s just a trend, it will pass, and at some point I’ll probably cave and upgrade when it starts actually affecting my ability to get work done, or more importantly get security updates. Once I adjust, I’ll stop noticing it, and life will go on.
As such, I wouldn’t normally find an obvious rebrand like this notable, much less feel like I had much to say about it. But then I happened to catch Apple’s behind-the-scenes video in my YouTube recommendations, and I realized I did have thoughts.

As Amazon blocks AI agents from shopping on its site, Walmart is taking the opposite approach, introducing new technology that lets AI agents make purchases on customers' behalf, with controls over spending and transaction approvals.
Walmart is embracing agentic commerce with the launch of its own Agent Gateway to manage transactions and other new features aimed at customers using AI agents, the retailer announced on Wednesday. The move comes shortly after Walmart’s top competitor, Amazon, began blocking AI agents from making purchases on behalf of online shoppers.
The company’s embrace of AI technology differentiates it from other online businesses, including not only Amazon but also various travel and booking sites, which have responded to the growing consumer adoption of AI agents by locking them out of their websites completely. Walmart, on the other hand, had already announced a partnership with a leading agent in the space, Meta’s Muse, and offers integrations with popular AI apps like ChatGPT, Gemini, and others.
Now, it’s expanding on those efforts with more technology to prepare for a world where AI agents become mainstream, said Walmart President and CEO John Furner, speaking at the Masters of Scale Summit in San Francisco on Wednesday.

items.t: NVIDIA Kumo Relational Outperforms Supervised Machine Learning on Relational Data, No Training Required
items.x:
NVIDIA Kumo Relational is a pre-trained relational foundation model that makes predictions directly on enterprise databases. Given a predictive query, it gathers up to 10,000 historical examples as context and predicts outcomes such as churn, demand, or fraud in a single forward pass. It needs no task-specific training, no feature engineering, and no flattening of tables. Kumo Relational is the first few-shot foundation model to outperform supervised machine learning on common relational benchmarks. Across 41 tasks on 15 databases, it beats supervised relational deep learning models and expert-engineered gradient-boosted tree pipelines, and on the SAP SALT enterprise benchmark it surpasses AutoGluon ensembles by 8% in mean reciprocal rank (MRR). It scales to databases with 500B+ rows and works for humans and agents alike, through NVIDIA's open-source, GPU-native structured-data-models library or as an NVIDIA NIM.
Foundation models have already rewritten the playbook for language and vision. Not long ago, production NLP meant a dedicated model per task, each fed by its own pipeline of tokenization, lemmatization, and n-grams.

items.t: Judge rejects Trump’s wild claim EPA can dismiss data center pollution lawsuits
items.d: Trump’s EPA can't unilaterally dismiss SpaceXAI pollution lawsuit, court rules.
items.x:
Elon Musk’s SpaceXAI is stuck facing a lawsuit over alleged data center pollution after Donald Trump failed to convince a judge that his Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has complete control over all Clean Air Act lawsuits and can dismiss any suit at whim.
Soon after unpermitted gas turbines were discovered powering Musk’s giant Colossus data center in Memphis, Tennessee, the NAACP sued . Its lawsuit sought an injunction requiring xAI (which, following a merger , is known now as SpaceXAI) to use the best available pollution control technology when operating the turbines and ordering penalties up to $124,426 per day per violation. Without such remedies, the turbines risked drastically spiking pollution in already vulnerable neighborhoods housing predominantly Black communities nearby, the NAACP argued.
To block the lawsuit, Trump tried to intervene, arguing that the EPA had the power to unilaterally dismiss lawsuits any time the president decides against enforcing the Clean Air Act. According to Trump, it would supposedly “not serve the public interest” if citizens were allowed to seek massive civil penalties to punish polluting AI firms that were trying to get data centers operational as fast as possible to support Trump’s AI Action Plan .

items.t: PHP Armageddon: OpenAI, Google’s Wiz find ancient holes, panicking the internet
items.d: This is the kind of security issue that was found and prevented by AI, but is also a high risk because of AI.
items.x:
This is the kind of security issue that was found and prevented by AI, but is also a high risk because of AI.
The U.S. National Security Agency’s sent out an alarming warning on Wednesday that two critical holes had been found in PHP, with patches already issued by the PHP Foundation.
PHP is a server-side programming language so widely used for web applications that it powers roughly 70% of the websites on the internet; by some accounts, that’s more than 33 million sites. It is also used by popular content management systems like WordPress.
The NSA warned that these holes are so severe that if a website can’t be patched immediately, it should be pulled off the web until it can be. The holes allow attackers to infiltrate the server’s file system or a database that may be used by the web app.
Interestingly, these holes have been tucked away in all versions of PHP since version 5, which was released in 2004. Websites not running relatively current versions of PHP will have some updating work to do, as PHP 8.1 and older versions are no longer supported. The recommendation is to update the web server to the current version of PHP, which is 8.5.12.
So how did two such ubiquitous, decades-old flaws that affect nearly every website on the internet suddenly come to light?

items.t: Train in Simulation, Deploy on a Real Robot: Microduck with Isaac Lab 3.0
items.x:
This post was written in collaboration with Antoine Pirrone, Augustin Crampette, Matthieu Lapeyre, Coralie Deplanne, Anne-Charlotte Passanisi, and Thomas Wolf.
Microduck is a newly released affordable open-source bipedal robot by Pollen Robotics and Hugging Face. And now you can train Microduck to walk with Isaac Lab and Newton. Test the policy, export it as ONNX, and deploy it on the real robot. Share it on the Hugging Face Hub or validate it for competition in Microduck Arena, then explore more advanced tasks with NVIDIA Isaac Lab.
A walking policy trained in simulation must also handle the friction, delays, and mechanical play of real robot servos.. NVIDIA Isaac Lab is an open-source framework for training policies across thousands of GPU-parallel simulations. With Newton, actuator modeling, and domain randomization, developers can prepare policies for real hardware. Microduck brings this workflow to life: train a walking policy in simulation, export it as ONNX, and deploy it on a real biped robot.
This tutorial walks you through training and evaluating Microduck with Isaac Lab and Newton, then exporting the policy for deployment.

items.t: How Specializing the Vocabulary of SLMs Can Cut Inference Cost by 77% in Real Applications
items.x:
Models specialized for a domain or a task by fine-tuning general open-source models, such as Qwen and Gemma, inherit a vocabulary built for many domains and general applications.
In an essay grader we run in production, that vocabulary split the text the model writes most into many tokens. This article previews some results from the VocabX paper, which we will publish soon: how we specialized the vocabulary around the cost of each token rather than its frequency, and cut measured inference cost by 77% without changing the base model.
The tokenizer is usually treated as a fixed property of the base model, inherited and left alone. For a model specialized in a single domain, it can be one of the largest cost levers, and it is set before any training step.
One of the systems we run in production is an automated grader for Portuguese essays, built on Qwen3-4B. It receives the essay, the prompt and the supporting texts, and returns a JSON assessment with a grade and a comment for each competency.
The model was already small, at 4 billion parameters, and had already been trained for the task. Its tokenizer, however, was still the original Qwen3-4B one, built for many languages and many kinds of text.

Blacksmith, a platform that helps companies more efficiently build and test software, including code written by AI, announced Wednesday a $66 million Series C funding round led by Sequoia that values the company at $1 billion.
In announcing the round, Blacksmith co-founder and CEO Aditya Jayaprakash said the company was founded to make continuous integration (CI) — the process of building, testing, merging, and validating code changes — “less painful.” In a blog post, he said that “most companies are struggling to keep up with the volume of CI they need to run,” especially in an era where so much code is written by AI.
“As agents write more of the world’s software, the question that matters is whether it can be trusted,” he added.
The company also announced that its annual recurring revenue has grown 17x and that it has run over 90 million CI jobs, or individual automated code checks. Customers include Mercury and Granola.
The Series C comes just two months after its $45 million Series B, which valued the company at $550 million.

items.t: Profiling TorchNeuron (Part 1): System-level profiling on AWS Trainium.
items.x:
Many ML practitioners have some intuition about how to make models run fast, but fewer know how to analyze why a model is slow. In Part 1 of this series, you will learn how to systematically analyze inference performance and identify where the time is spent.
This post starts from scratch and assumes no prior profiling experience. The walkthrough uses AWS Trainium, a purpose-built AI chip for deep learning training and inference workloads, and TorchNeuron, its open source native PyTorch backend. TorchNeuron supports standard PyTorch workflows on Trainium, including eager execution, torch.compile, and standard PyTorch APIs, with minimal code changes. Additionally, TorchNeuron integrates with Neuron Kernel Interface (NKI) to enable custom operators and performance optimization for Trainium hardware. By the end, you should know:
Before you profile a workload, it helps to understand how Neuron integrates with PyTorch.
The Neuron backend uses PyTorch's PrivateUse1 extension point. This mechanism lets an accelerator integrate with the framework without adding a dedicated dispatch key such as cuda. The torch_neuronx package works with upstream PyTorch to register Neuron as a native backend for PyTorch code.

Miami-based OpenEvidence, founded by serial entrepreneur Daniel Nadler in 2022, said that many of America’s 1 million physicians processed more than 42 million prompts last month. Doctors are using the company’s chatbot to scour medical journals and clinical guidelines to help diagnose and treat patients.
The ads-powered platform has grown largely by word of mouth, penetrating a sector where few tools have seen similar traction. “We’re the first viral consumer internet app in healthcare,” Nadler told the FT in an interview.

items.t: Granite Speech 5.0: Transcribe, Translate, and Attribute more Accurately and Faster
items.x:
We're excited to share three updates to IBM's Granite Speech collection: a new speech-language model, granite-speech-5.0-2b, and revised versions of two models the community already uses, granite-speech-5.0-470m-turboctc and granite-speech-4.1-2b-plus. Together they cover the full range of enterprise speech work: transcription and translation with high accuracy, extremely fast transcription at the edge, and recordings where who spoke, and when, matter as much as what was said.
granite-speech-5.0-2b is the successor to granite-speech-4.1-2b at the same parameter count. It transcribes English, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese, and Japanese, and translates to and from English in those languages, plus English to Italian and Mandarin. It was trained on 390,000 hours of public audio, plus synthetic data built for Japanese ASR, keyword biasing, and translation.
The model ships under Apache 2.0 with support in Transformers, vLLM, llama.cpp, and mlx-audio for Apple Silicon.
Chart 1: granite-speech-5.0-2b ranks #2 among top open-weight ASR models on average English WER (5.06%). Lower is better.

items.t: AI promises productivity, but for managers, it’s mostly a headache for now
items.d: More than 50% of managers say they're finding it harder to evaluate employees' work after adopting AI, according to a new survey.
items.x:
More than 50% of managers say they're finding it harder to evaluate employees' work after adopting AI, according to a new survey.
Companies are giving employees AI tools to make them more productive, but the tools appear to be creating new problems for their managers.
More than half of senior leaders say they find it harder to evaluate employees’ work after adopting AI, according to a Nielsen survey of 1,700 directors and senior managers across seven countries, commissioned by work-management company Monday.com. The reason is that much of employees’ output now arrives polished in the manager’s inbox, making it hard to tell how much came from the employee and how much from AI. As a result, nearly half of managers say they spend more time reviewing and guiding their teams’ output than they used to.
That’s not to say managers are unhappy about AI. Quite the opposite, in fact: 94% of the managers polled said they were excited to improve work using AI, and many are confident they know where to use it to get the most value.

items.t: NVIDIA Kumo Forecast Combines Pretrained Time-Series Representations with Historical Pattern Retrieval and Interpretability
items.x:
NVIDIA Kumo Forecast (formerly known as NV-Tesseract Forecasting) is a multi-variate time-series forecasting model that combines a pretrained Transformer backbone with Domain-Aware Representation and Retrieval (DARR), a context-enhanced forecasting mode that blends direct model predictions with patterns retrieved from historical data. This includes interpretability of the results. Built on the MOMENT-1-large backbone, Kumo Forecast uses an approximately 340-million-parameter base encoder plus a trainable forecasting head.
The library provides a DataFrame-first API, configurable forecast horizons, optional historical context for retrieval, and an interpretability framework that produces horizon-specific explanations without modifying the underlying forecaster.
A forecasting system can draw on two different sources of information: representations learned during pretraining and historical observations available for the current application. Kumo-Forecast brings these together through a pretrained forecasting model and an optional retrieval pathway over historical context.
In its direct forecasting path, Kumo-Forecast uses a MOMENT-based Transformer and a trained forecasting head to predict future values.

items.t: Protein Design with RFD4-Proteina and Hugging Face Spaces
items.x:
Protein design starts with setting a goal: a target to bind, a molecule to recognize, or an arrangement of atoms to preserve. Turning that goal into a design has usually meant splitting up the workflow across models that each handle one modality or one stage and reassembling the pieces afterward. Information is lost at every handoff.
RFD4-Proteina is a BioNeMo open model for programmable protein design, co-developed by NVIDIA and the University of Washington's Institute for Protein Design. It brings protein sequence and all-atom structure generation into one model, reducing the handoffs between separate backbone, sequence, and all-atom structure design models. It can generate proteins in molecular contexts that include other proteins, small molecules, nucleic acids, glycans, metal ions, and modified amino acids (e.g., a phosphorylated residue on a target protein).
RFD4-Proteina pairs a flow-matching model with an autoencoder. The autoencoder represents each standard or modified amino acid, sugar, DNA, or RNA nucleotide as an anchor-atom coordinate (for amino acids, the alpha carbon) and a learned latent vector encoding its chemical identity and local geometry.

items.t: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Embed, Rerank, and Parse: Advancing Agents with World-Class Retrieval Models
items.x:
An agent’s answers depend on the evidence it can retrieve. When that evidence is incomplete or irrelevant, the agent will repeat searches and inspect additional documents, consuming more inference tokens before completing the task. Better retrieval can help agents reach grounded answers with fewer wasted tokens. At enterprise scale, that waste leads to massive inefficiencies. Agents need the right retrieval models and systems to reach insights faster.
Today, we are expanding the Nemotron Retriever collection with new open, commercially available models for embedding, reranking, and document extraction. The new models include Nemotron 3.5 Embed 8B BF16, 1B BF16, 1B NVFP4, Nemotron 3.5 Rerank 8B BF16, and Nemotron 3.5 Parse at 631M parameters.
Together, these state-of-the-art models bring multimodal retrieval, relevance ranking, and document processing to enterprise agent workflows.
Retrieval quality affects both the answers an agent produces and the LLM inference cost. Relevant evidence can help the agent answer a question or better decide its next step, and reranking improves the quality of evidence that enters its context.
Consider an agent asked to identify products at risk of stockouts next quarter and explain why.

items.x:
Editor’s note: This article was written by Lucia, a TechNode reporter.
Building a more capable AI model is only half the battle. The other half is making it affordable to run at scale. DeepSeek announced a V4.1 Flash update aimed at faster task completion and shorter outputs, alongside an open-source framework for more efficient inference.
A Model Update With Promising Early Results
On October 17, DeepSeek released V4.1-Flash-1017 , an update to its V4.1 Flash model. The company's published benchmark results show improvements in several areas, including coding and agentic tasks. For example, its Terminal-Bench 4.0 score rose from 31.2 to 42.3, while DeepSWE v1.1 increased from 74.2 to 77.0.
A cost-performance chart for the DeepSWE v1.1 coding benchmark shows V4.1 Flash-1017 achieving a 77% Pass@1 score at about $0.20 per task, outperforming several models that cost substantially more to run. At lower-cost settings of $0.11–$0.14 per task, it still scores around 72–73%.
DeepSeek also reports shorter task execution times and outputs, which can reduce inference costs when a model completes the same work using fewer tokens and less computing time.

items.t: Ant Group and vLLM Open-Source Humming, Quantized Inference Kernels With Zhenwu 810E Support
items.d: Ant Group and the vLLM community open-sourced Humming, a JIT GEMM kernel library for quantized inference. It covers INT1-8 and FP4-FP8 mixes and fully supports T-Head's Zhenwu 810E.
items.x:
Ant Group and the vLLM community have open-sourced Humming, a just-in-time compiled GEMM kernel library for quantized large language model inference. The project is released under Apache 2.0 from Ant Group's inclusionAI organization and mirrored under the vLLM project.
Humming aims at a common problem in quantized serving: every mix of weight bit width, activation format, scaling scheme, dense versus mixture-of-experts layout, and GPU generation tends to need its own specialized kernel. The library converts supported export formats into a shared quantization description, then JIT-compiles kernels from reusable CUDA components for the target shape, device and compute options.
According to the project, one architecture covers integer weights from INT1 to INT8 and floating-point weights from FP4 to FP8, paired with FP16, BF16, FP8, FP4, INT8 or INT4 activations where the formats are compatible. It supports both dense GEMM and MoE GEMM, and targets NVIDIA GPUs from Turing onward. Dependencies are limited to PyTorch and NVCC, and the pip package is described as only about 100 KB.
A China-primary angle is hardware reach beyond NVIDIA.

items.t: METASTONE Launches TokenFleet to Schedule LLM Inference Across GPU Clusters and Data Centers
items.d: Compute operator METASTONE unveiled TokenFleet, a scheduling framework for LLM inference clusters. Its slides show P95 time-to-first-token down 32.4% and on-target output throughput up about 29.4%.
items.x:
METASTONE, an independent compute operator, has introduced TokenFleet, a distributed scheduling framework for large language model inference. The company announced it during the 2026 CCF National High Performance Computing Conference.
TokenFleet does not make individual models run faster. Instead it targets cluster-level problems: requests piling up on some GPU instances while capacity sits idle elsewhere, long-document jobs crowding out real-time chat, and timeouts or cancellations that burn compute without producing a usable answer. METASTONE frames the goal as raising effective token output, meaning tokens from requests that finish successfully and meet their service targets.
The framework has three parts. TokenPilot picks an instance inside a model pool. It weighs the gain from reusing a cached prompt prefix, which skips repeated prefill computation, against the cost of waiting in a longer queue on that instance. It estimates workload from input size, output budget and reusable prefix, then scores candidates using queue depth, in-flight tokens, KV cache pressure and predicted latency.
FleetMind handles routing across data centers.

items.t: SenseTime Open-Sources SenseNova-RoboRSI Embodied AI Harness and a 27B Robot Brain Model
items.d: SenseTime open-sourced the SenseNova-RoboRSI evaluation harness and a 27B embodied model, after a study of GPT-6-Astra across 12 simulated benchmarks and 8 real robots. Figures are SenseTime's own.
items.x:
SenseTime has open-sourced SenseNova-RoboRSI, a framework for evaluating embodied AI systems, together with an embodied model called SenseNova-RoboRSI-27B-Preview. The release follows a study in which SenseTime tested the large model GPT-6-Astra on 12 simulated robot benchmarks and 8 physical robots. All results below come from SenseTime's own tests.
SenseTime says that when it gave GPT-6-Astra access to training demonstrations and raised step limits to as much as 10 times the official settings, the model saturated the LIBERO and SIMPLE benchmarks and reached an 81.9% success rate on RoboDojo. In one case, nine RoboDojo tasks that had failed in all five attempts succeeded in all five once the model was simply allowed to keep interacting.
The cost was high. In SenseTime's extended-budget tests, stacking bowls took about 131 minutes and roughly $19 in estimated inference costs, while putting a pen into a pen holder took 263 minutes and about $55. SenseTime also found that GPT-6-Astra remained weakest on long-horizon tasks, struggled to transfer skills across tasks, and had trouble with deformable objects and fine control on real robots.
The company then tested pairing a slow reasoning model with a fast action model.

He brings to the Trust decades of scientific expertise across observational cosmology and precision measurement. He has also advised the US government on national security and arms control. “I am honored to join Anthropic’s Long-Term Benefit Trust and to help the company deliver on its public benefit mission,” said Stubbs. “I use AI tools in my research every day and see what they make possible, and as an educator I have confronted some of the hard questions they raise. As a grandfather, I want to help ensure that AI is developed and deployed for the long-term benefit of humanity.” Stubbs is the Samuel C. Moncher Professor of Physics and of Astronomy at Harvard, where he served as Dean of Science from 2018 to 2024. In 1998, as a member of the High-Z Supernova Search Team, he helped discover the accelerating expansion of the universe, work that later earned the team the Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics. He was also the inaugural project scientist for what is now the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, which started a 10-year survey of the southern sky in June. One of its aims is to study the accelerating expansion he helped discover.

It’s available as a standalone app on iOS and Android, and on claude.ai. For this research preview, Claude Duet is included in Pro and Max plans and uses the same usage limits as the rest of Claude. To get access, join the waitlist (opens in new tab).
We designed Claude Duet to be a partner you can trust. Professionals of all kinds have to juggle many decisions a day, and we think they’ll find Claude Duet most useful. It helps you prioritize where to spend your time and energy, and to leave room for the ambitious projects that felt impossible or daunting before.
What makes Claude Duet so helpful is its judgment.

The proposed policy seems to offer protections against AI run amok but actually forbids federal agencies from blocking a model's release without the permission of a judge.
Over the past year, concerns have swirled over the potential dangers posed by artificial intelligence, and debates have raged over the proper path for AI safety. Now, Anthropic appears to have put forth its own vision for how the government might regulate its industry.
Politico recently reported that the AI lab has been shopping around a new draft bill on AI safety that it hopes Congress might consider adopting. The legislation posits certain scenarios in which the release of an AI model could be blocked from distribution.
Those scenarios involve a “foreseeable, imminent risk” — one in which over 50 people are at risk of dying or if over a billion dollars in property damage could result, Politico writes.

items.x:
Anthropic is reportedly struggling to secure enough compute from cloud providers that increasingly view it as a competitor, even as its infrastructure spending balloons ahead of a planned November IPO.
Anthropic is having trouble securing enough cloud capacity from AWS, Google, and Microsoft, which increasingly see the Claude-maker as a competitor rather than a customer, according to an S-1 filing leaked to The Wall Street Journal.
The leaked filing provides more color to the numbers Reuters and the Financial Times reported in late September, including that Anthropic believes it could spend more $750 billion on cloud contracts, some of which includes deals still in negotiation.
And still, that is not enough. Anthropic is leasing its own data centers and working with third-party data center operators. But the firm worries those operators have a “limited operating history,” which could make them less reliable than the hyperscalers.
Anthropic’s enormous spend comes on the back of an $80.7 billion net loss in the first half of the year.

OpenAI says it's adding Orchestra's team and technology to work on Rosalind, its AI model for life sciences research, and to its related Rosalind Workbench tool, a harness that aims to help researchers plan experiments and analyze results.
OpenAI on Tuesday acquired a four-year-old AI biotech software startup called Orchestra Bio, the company announced via its website. Terms of the deal were not disclosed, but the startup had reportedly raised around $20 million as of 2025 from backers like Andreessen Horowitz, Atria, and 8VC.
Orchestra creates AI agents that help biotech companies manage the minutiae of drug discovery operations, from tracking finances to resolving scheduling issues with clinical trials.
OpenAI says it’s adding Orchestra’s team and technology to work on Rosalind, its AI model for life sciences research, and to its related Rosalind Workbench tool, a harness that aims to help researchers plan experiments and analyze results. OpenAI has already won some big names as customers for Rosalind, including, it says, Moderna⁠ and Novo Nordisk⁠.
The acquisition is a classic example of how the biggest AI labs (namely OpenAI and Anthropic) are building ever more software for the biggest industries, like pharma.

items.t: Gemini's Personal Intelligence is coming to cars
items.d: It's probably time to audit your Gemini settings.
items.x:
Google kicked off 2026 with the addition of Personal Intelligence to Gemini, allowing its AI to pull in more of your data to formulate answers. It started as a paid feature but eventually came to all Gemini users. However, this feature wasn't available in the car until now. Google is rolling out Personal Intelligence to Android Auto and Google Built-in, and it is still, thankfully, an optional feature.
As Google points out , a generative AI's outputs are better "when it knows the world and knows you," which is correct in an uncomfortable sort of way. The more context you can provide to a model, the better the output will be at the end of the token shuffle. Since Google has so much of your data already, it sees Personal Intelligence as a differentiator versus other AI systems. You don't have to provide the AI context because it already has it from apps like Gmail and Calendar.
Personal Intelligence is beginning its rollout in Android Auto today, and it will come to vehicles with Google built-in in the next few months. As an aside, "Google built-in" is questionable branding, but it refers to cars that run Google software in the infotainment system rather than projecting an interface from your phone.

items.t: Google has joined Amazon in attacking Nvidia’s stronghold with AI app developers
items.d: Google has joined Amazon in releasing a developer tool that makes it easy for PyTorch users to move their apps off Nvidia GPUs.
items.x:
Google has joined Amazon in releasing a developer tool that makes it easy for PyTorch users to move their apps off Nvidia GPUs.
On Tuesday, Google announced that TorchTPU, its long-awaited version of PyTorch, is now available as an open-source project. With this, Google joins Amazon in trying to break Nvidia’s stranglehold on the AI industry, where most AI apps are written by default to run on Nvidia’s chips, or GPUs.
PyTorch is the popular open-source toolkit that AI app developers and startups use to build, train, and run AI models. It is, by some accounts, used by 85% of the AI apps. PyTorch was originally developed by Meta (then Facebook) in 2016, long before the world had an inkling that LLMs would change the world. At the time, Nvidia’s GPUs were already the standard hardware for AI research, so many of PyTorch’s features were built to work specifically with them. In 2022, Meta turned PyTorch over to the Linux Foundation, a nonprofit that manages many important open source projects.
Google’s version, TorchTPU, lets AI apps run on Google’s AI chips, called Tensor Processing Units (TPUs). It also makes it easy to move existing PyTorch apps to TPUs and, therefore, to Google Cloud.

OpenAI announced on Tuesday that users can now lock ChatGPT conversations to keep sensitive chats private when others may have access to their screen or device. Users can secure their locked chats with a four-digit PIN, or use Face ID or Touch ID on supported devices.
Unlike the app’s Temporary Chats, which provide a separate session that doesn’t appear in chat history, users can return to Locked Chats at any time.
The addition of locked chats adds a new layer of privacy to ChatGPT, as the app is increasingly used for personal conversations.

items.t: Ukraine’s drone rescue of wounded soldier puts much touted idea into practice
items.d: Ukraine’s latest drone innovation may boost bleak odds of evacuating casualties.
items.x:
Ukraine’s unprecedented drone rescue of a wounded soldier from the battlefield has shown once again how battlefield necessity can spur innovation. The operation was revealed just days after separate Ukrainian drones designed for casualty evacuation were deployed for frontline testing—taking a step beyond the US military’s decades of experimentation with similar concepts.
The drone evacuation of the injured soldier took place at an undisclosed time and place on the frontline where the presence of Russian drones and landmines made it impractical to send in a wheeled ground robot , according to The Kyiv Independent . On October 19, Ukraine’s Army shared a video of the drone evacuation, showing the wounded soldier securing himself in a harness suspended beneath a heavy hexacopter drone with six rotors before being flown to safety.
“This is a historic event, the next stage of evacuating the wounded, which we will all come to,” said Napalm, a programmer of the 92nd separate assault brigade's unmanned ground systems company, who went by his callsign per Ukrainian military practice, in a statement. “Now the serious systematic work begins, so that such missions are carried out constantly.”
