items.t: Eric Schmidt reportedly owns about half as much of Anthropic as CEO Dario Amodei
items.d: Eric Schmidt’s fortune is about to get even bigger.
items.x:
The former Google CEO owns about 1% stake in the leading AI lab, Bloomberg reported.
Eric Schmidt’s fortune is about to get even bigger. The former Google CEO is reported to own about 1% of Anthropic after investing tens of millions of dollars in the leading AI lab’s Series A round in 2021, according to Bloomberg. The startup was valued at $461 million at the time, according to PitchBook data.
If Bloomberg’s estimate is accurate, Schmidt’s stake is remarkably large compared with the 2% of the company that co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei holds. Anthropic is widely expected to go public before the end of the year, with top-end market estimates valuing the company at as much as $2 trillion. At that valuation, Schmidt would add as much as $20 billion to his net worth, which Bloomberg currently puts at $57.5 billion.
Schmidt has been an active tech investor since stepping down as Google CEO in 2011. He deploys capital through multiple entities, including Tomorrow Ventures, Innovation Endeavors Management, and his family office, Hillspire.

items.t: Meta tries to scapegoat staff who downloaded torrents to spare execs
items.d: Meta argues nobody “decided” to pirate books to train AI.
items.x:
In copyright lawsuits over AI training, Meta has spent weeks blaming staff for downloading torrents. The company has now been ordered to name executives who authorized decisions to pirate books from shadow libraries like Anna’s Archive and LibGen, TorrentFreak reported .
In a discovery order impacting a class action raised by book authors—including Richard Kadrey and Sarah Silverman—as well as a lawsuit from publisher Entrepreneur Media, Magistrate Judge Thomas Hixon largely agreed that Meta must clearly identify key decision makers. Following testimony from Meta staff who downloaded torrents, the order could expose a wider range of supervisors, managers, and executives whom staffers said greenlit the piracy.
Meta had been hoping to avoid detailing the chain of command, particularly for leadership involved in early AI training. According to a Meta court filing , its initial efforts to compile massive AI datasets were managed through an “informal approach" where supposedly nobody with authority made any decisions. Instead, Meta insisted that a “decision” was “made only in the sense” that some staffers “technically” downloaded torrents.

items.t: Meta’s Muse hits 10M US downloads in 40 days, a milestone reached by only 11 other apps
items.d: New data also shows Muse is retaining users at higher rates than its AI rivals.
items.x:
Meta's AI companion Muse has surpassed 10 million U.S. downloads in its first 40 days, joining an exclusive group of apps that includes Threads. New data also shows Muse is retaining users at higher rates than its AI rivals.
Meta’s AI companion, Muse, is now one of only a dozen mobile apps to have reached 10 million U.S. downloads in its first 40 days on the market. According to new data from market intelligence provider Sensor Tower, Muse has seen 10.9 million downloads since its September debut, 10.2 million of which were in the United States.
Only 11 other apps to date have reached this type of post-launch milestone, said Sensor Tower’s Senior Insights Analyst Kara Lee. The most recent of these was Meta’s Threads, back in July 2023. Other apps that saw this kind of scale were largely mobile games, Lee noted.
Meta’s success is tied to the company’s ability to scale its new apps by marketing them across its other services, which it has done with both Threads and Muse. Threads was built on top of Instagram’s social graph, and its content has been integrated into both Facebook and Instagram.

items.t: Ex-Nvidia-turned-VC Amulya Vishwanath: ‘Physical AI is in its LEGO era’
items.d: It’s the moment everyone is waiting for — the ChatGPT moment for robotics, Amulya Vishwanath explained to TechCrunch’s Equity.
items.x:
It’s the moment everyone is waiting for — the ChatGPT moment for robotics, Amulya Vishwanath explained to TechCrunch’s Equity.
She is the founder and managing partner of Techable Ventures, a VC firm focused on physical AI, which she started after spending nearly seven years as a product marketer at Nvidia. Before that, she held the same role at a company that was later bought by Intel and was a digital signal processing engineer at Interconnect Systems, which was later bought by the electronics manufacturer Molex.
She stopped by Equity to talk about the future of physical AI — one of the industry’s latest buzzwords.
“A lot of companies and experts have been talking about the ChatGPT moment for robotics,” she said, adding that right now the industry was more in a “LEGO era.”
“There are a lot of foundational software and building blocks for robotics that are being rethought right now as we speak, and it’s super important in order for innovation to scale,” she continued.
Right now, people are building the basics — the robotic hands or the actuators — that can one day come together and build that big-ticket-item, like a bunch of LEGOs coming together.

items.t: FairStress: A deeper evaluation of fairness in LLM decision-making
items.x:
Measuring fairness beyond the final answer Models do not always hold correct answers equally Why existing benchmarks can produce a different result Training for symmetric robustness Can existing fixes help? From fair outcomes to fair decision-making 📄 Tech Report | 🤗 Data | 💻 Code
Today we’re introducing FairStress, a benchmark for measuring demographic fairness in LLMs beyond the choice a model ultimately makes in decisions impacting people. FairStress is available for download, and we’re also building it into Olmo-eval, our open workbench for running and comparing model evaluations.
Models are increasingly being used in high-stakes settings where their outputs can affect people’s opportunities, resources, and care, from screening job applicants and approving loans to prioritizing patients for treatment and evaluating students for admissions. Standard demographic fairness benchmarks often test whether a model selects the same candidate in otherwise identical scenarios after the candidates’ demographic identities are swapped.

items.t: Plants can speak using electricity, so this startup built an AI model to decipher their language
items.d: Electric Plant has built an AI-powered translator to help humans listen to what plants are saying with the subtle electricity coursing through their stems.
items.x:
Electric Plant has built an AI-powered translator to help humans listen to what plants are saying with the subtle electricity coursing through their stems.
A few years ago, Mast was reading through some scientific literature when he stumbled upon research about a houseplant wired to a motorized stand. When the plant wanted more light, electrical signals flowed through the living tissues. A control board sensed the current and wheeled the plant closer to the light source.
“I’m like, what the heck?” Mast told TechCrunch. “That was the entry to the rabbit hole for me.”
Mast wound up partnering with Lee von Kraus, a neuroscientist who has worked with DARPA, to found Electric Plant, which has been spending the past three years collecting data to build a large language model, Bombadil, capable of interpreting the subtle electrical signals coursing through a plant’s stem and relaying details about the plant’s needs to growers.
The founders believe their model could one day lead to a tool that would let people “speak” to plants.

items.t: The new economics of enterprise AI
items.d: Imagine your company just discovered electricity. At first only a few machines run on it, and nobody worries about efficiency — consumption is low and the value is obvious. But once electricity becomes infrastructure, every process depends…
items.x:
Imagine your company just discovered electricity. At first only a few machines run on it, and nobody worries about efficiency — consumption is low and the value is obvious. But once electricity becomes infrastructure, every process depends on it, and the question changes from “can we use it?” to “how efficiently are we using it?”
Enterprise AI is going through the same shift. What began as isolated chatbot and copilot experiments is becoming a foundational layer of the business, with models, agents, and data increasingly interconnected in production workloads. The important question stops being what a token or GPU-hour costs. It becomes how efficiently the AI environment converts paid capacity into useful business outcomes.
That’s the metric worth tracking: effective cost per useful outcome — the total platform, model, operations, and capacity cost required to complete work the business can actually use, whether a resolved request or a completed workflow.
Utilization is central to the economics. Directing more work to paid-for capacity lowers effective unit cost; idle GPUs, fragmented workloads, and oversized models all raise the cost of every useful result. Enterprises generally choose among three models:
A bespoke stack — procuring infrastructure and controls in-house.

items.t: ALTK-Evolve: How learned memory tops the τ²-bench leaderboard on customer service tasks without a frontier model
items.x:
Learned memory takes a basic ReAct agent with GPT-4.1 to the top τ²-bench tests policy-bound customer service Guidelines improve capability and reliability The best amount of guidance depends on the domain Better performance costs more tokens, not more turns Learned guidelines also improve agents using frontier models ALTK-Evolve tops the leaderboard comparison Agents can improve without weight updates Links: ALTK-Evolve learns and applies a playbook using GPT-4.1, outperforming the retail entries on τ²-bench, a customer service agent benchmark—without updating model weights.
Using GPT-4.1, an older, non-reasoning model, a basic customer-service agent reaches 67.5% Pass^4 on τ²-bench retail — meaning it solves the task on all four independent attempts for 67.5% of tasks. It scores above every retail entry in our October 12, 2026 leaderboard snapshot. It runs on the benchmark's stock ReAct scaffold, with learned guidelines appended to its system prompt.
ALTK-Evolve builds that playbook using GPT-4.1. It analyzes the agent's training-task attempts and uses the model to distill successes and failures into short behavioral rules: how to authenticate a customer, confirm a transaction, or handle a return.

At the design company’s first Config conference held in India, the company announced 20 new model context protocol (MCP) partners, including Amp, ClickUp, Dia, Junie by JetBrains, Linear, Meta Muse, Mistral, Notion, OpenCode, and Sarvam Agents.

“I find it interesting that Anthropic (creators of MCP standard) do not expose artifacts / other cloud resources created via MCP,” he wrote on X. “The debate is framed as open vs closed. Everyone always prefers open… obviously. And meanwhile issues of asymmetric context sharing are ignored.”

items.t: US orders federal agencies to remove China’s DeepSeek AI from their systems
items.d: The U.S. has ordered federal civilian agencies to remove DeepSeek products and third-party services built using its technology, citing national security concerns.
items.x:
The US has ordered federal civilian agencies to remove DeepSeek products and third-party services built using its technology, citing national security concerns.
The U.S. has ordered federal civilian agencies to stop purchasing services and products developed by Chinese AI startup DeepSeek and remove them from government IT systems over national security concerns tied to the Chinese AI startup’s operations in China, according to the Department of Homeland Security. The order goes beyond banning DeepSeek’s own product, but also covers third-party products and services built using DeepSeek technology, though agencies can request exceptions.
The DHS raised concerns about DeepSeek’s handling of user data, warning that sensitive information from US government users could potentially be accessible to Chinese authorities under Chinese law, the order said.
The move comes amid intensifying tech competition in AI between the US and China. The Chinese AI model challenges its U.S. rivals, including OpenAI and Meta, with low-cost open-weight models.
China pushed back against the U.S.’s move. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said Tuesday that Beijing opposes “overstretching the concept of national security and politicizing technology and trade issues,” according to an official briefing.

items.t: Eka is worth $1.45B thanks to a physical AI model that has experts raving
items.d: Eka Robotics may be the first robotic arm that is actually good at picking up a wide range of objects, and it is so smooth and human-like, it is wowing the industry.
items.x:
Eka Robotics may be the first robotic arm that is actually good at picking a wide range of objects up, and it is so smooth and human-like, it is wowing the industry.
Robots still aren’t that good at picking things up, despite billions of dollars of investment and endless videos fed into deep learning models.
That may be about to change, thanks to a manipulation architecture built by Eka Robotics, which encompasses a force-sensitive gripper and a new kind of deep-learning model. Founded by MIT professor Pulkit Agrawal and former Google DeepMind researcher Tuomas Haarnoja, the startup just closed an $150 million Series A round that values it at $1.45 billion post-money, led by venture funds a16z and F-Prime.
“They are already exceeding superhuman performance for certain tasks, and so we think over the next few months there will be superhuman performance in many dexterous manipulation tasks,” Raghu Raguram, the a16z general partner who co-led the fundraising round, told TechCrunch.
In an era of never-ending robotic demonstrations, Eka’s capabilities are shocking veteran robot builders.
Kris Hauser, a professor at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, said it had a “wow factor” compared to other robot demos he saw recently.

Muse, the new general-purpose AI agent from Meta, can expose sensitive information when users share conversations through Web links, researchers reported Monday.
Like many online services, Muse allows users to share searches, conversations, images, and similar content with other people. Such share features usually involve clicking an option to create a unique URL that anyone can use to load a page hosting the content. To keep potentially sensitive information from being accessible to unintended people, the URLs typically contain a long sequence of text that can’t be easily guessed.
Muse, which Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said last month was “built from the ground up for privacy and security,” seems to take the same precautions. But a central design decision for constructing URLs has made the links easy to discover. As a result, researchers from security firm Claroc said they were able to enumerate 6,800 links Muse users created for sharing conversations with others. items.t: AI adoption by industry shows what other sectors can learn
items.d: The current narrative around artificial intelligence in the workplace is largely driven by Silicon Valley. But treating the tech sector as an island misses the actual trends in technology adoption–tech is just the first industry in line…
items.x:
The current narrative around artificial intelligence in the workplace is largely driven by Silicon Valley. But treating the tech sector as an island misses the actual trends in technology adoption–tech is just the first industry in line.
As generative AI and automation tools mature, the shifts currently reshaping software engineering and product management will inevitably filter into healthcare, education, retail, and manufacturing. The variation in adoption rates today isn’t a sign that non-tech industries are falling behind, but rather a reflection of the different speeds at which industries absorb new workflows. For leaders and their teams outside of tech, this differential pace provides a practical blueprint for how AI adoption unfolds, and where the opportunities lie.
Recent survey data from TripleTen highlights just how stark the current adoption curve is across different sectors of the economy (see Figure 1).
Figure 1: The AI adoption curve remains steep across industries, but non-tech industry adoption rates are increasing.
While tech leads the way, finance emerges as a clear second: 48% of finance workers have been asked to use AI chatbots, and 32% have been asked to automate parts of their workflow.

items.x:
Yelp is embedding numerous new AI features into its app that can do everything from call to check on restaurant wait times to create personalized recommendations that remember your preferences.
Over the last few weeks, personal assistants like Instinct, Fo, and Muse have enabled users to call businesses for customer support and appointment booking. Following this trend, Yelp is adding the ability for its app users to get a voice agent to call a restaurant to check wait times.
The new feature, Check for Me, will show up on restaurant pages in the app, where users can enter their party size and phone number. The AI agent then calls on behalf of the user to check wait times and texts them the results to decide if they want to go to that particular restaurant.
Last year, Yelp debuted its voice solution for restaurants and service providers. With this new feature, the discovery platform is fulfilling the consumer side of the equation, though there is a possibility that a user’s agent will talk to the restaurant’s agent, and agent-to-agent communication might break down the conversation.
The company is also updating its Yelp AI assistant that helps users discover restaurants and services.

Required for a complete inference service (not included in this release):

items.t: A visit to Samsung’s massive new semiconductor hub
items.d: Generative AI models run on powerful chips known as GPUs, which depend on stacks of specialized memory chips packaged with the processor. To meet growing demand for memory, Samsung is building a massive new semiconductor manufacturing…
items.x:
Generative AI models run on powerful chips known as GPUs, which depend on stacks of specialized memory chips packaged with the processor. To meet growing demand for memory, Samsung is building a massive new semiconductor manufacturing complex in Pyeongtaek, South Korea. Three fabs already operate around the clock, and a fourth is coming online. Construction of a fifth was halted during a drop in demand for memory chips in 2024 but restarted when the AI boom sent demand soaring.
It’s just before noon on a Monday, and construction workers are pouring out of Samsung’s fabs in Pyeongtaek, a farming city south of Seoul where rice paddies abut a sprawling chipmaking complex. Thousands of workers, dressed head to toe in black with sky-blue vests, take off helmets bearing their names and fab numbers.
They walk to lunch, sweaty and flushed, in chunky sneakers capped with yellow rubber toe guards. Some hop on scooters or motorcycles to get around the campus, which covers an area about the size of New York City’s Central Park. They’ll dine at buffets, diners, and beef stew joints, walking past banners advertising short-term leases for studio apartments.

items.t: What if AI could remember your adventures for you? Souvi is exploring the idea
items.d: As more AI hardware focuses on voice assistants, information processing, and workplace productivity, one Chinese startup is taking a different approach by using AI to help people preserve their life experiences. Shanghai-based Vibe…
items.x:
As more AI hardware focuses on voice assistants, information processing, and workplace productivity, one Chinese startup is taking a different approach by using AI to help people preserve their life experiences.
Shanghai-based Vibe Technology has introduced Souvi, an outdoor AI memory device designed for activities such as hiking, camping, travel, and urban exploration. By combining low-interruption recording with AI-powered content processing, the product aims to turn scattered photos and videos into more complete personal memories.
Unlike traditional action cameras, which primarily focus on capturing footage, Souvi centers on a different question: When a trip ends, what can people actually take away from the experience?
“We focus on AI and personal memory because AI can help people work more efficiently while giving them new ways to preserve their life experiences,” Deng Jiawei, the company’s CEO, said in an interview with TechNode.
For many people, travel offers countless moments worth remembering, but capturing and organizing them takes effort. Taking photos can distract people from the experience, while sorting through footage, organizing timelines, and editing videos afterward can be time-consuming.

ACE Robotics, founded by SenseTime co-founder Xiaogang Wang, released its ACE-Brain-0.6 embodied AI model on October 19. Built through supervised fine-tuning of Qwen3.5-9B, the model focuses on identifying objects, locating them in images and determining where a robot can interact with them.

items.t: Stars Micro System Unveils C82-4G PCIe 6.0 Switch, an 800G AI NIC and a Multi-Mode RAID Chip
items.d: Wuxi-based Stars Micro System launched the C82-4G, which it calls China's first PCIe 6.0 switch, with up to 144 lanes at 64 GT/s, plus an 800G multi-protocol AI NIC and a multi-mode RAID chip.
items.x:
WuXi Stars Micro System Technologies has introduced three interconnect chips aimed at AI servers and clusters. The company, founded in 2020, held its first brand and full-stack product launch in Wuxi on October 15, showing 12 interconnect chips already in mass production alongside the new parts.
The centerpiece is the C82-4G, which the company calls the first PCIe 6.0 switch developed in China. It supports up to 144 lanes at 64 GT/s per lane, double the per-lane rate of PCIe 5.0, using PAM4 signaling and FLIT mode. The company quotes non-blocking switching with latency in the 100-nanosecond range, and support for fabric networking plus CXL memory expansion and pooling. It is designed for internal connections inside next-generation AI servers, where switches extend a CPU's PCIe lanes to GPUs, network cards and SSDs.
The second product is an 800G multi-protocol AI network interface card, which the company describes as the first of its kind from a Chinese supplier. It integrates a 48-lane PCIe Gen6 switch, supports 800G line-rate forwarding with microsecond-level latency, offloads RoCE v2 and offers programmable congestion control.

items.t: China Telecom Open-Sources Xing4.0-29B-Intent to Turn Commands Into Structured Parameters
items.d: China Telecom's XingChen lab released Xing4.0-29B-Intent, which classifies intents and fills structured arguments in one JSON output, along with 2.75 million training samples and an inference SDK.
items.x:
The XingChen AGI lab at China Telecom Artificial Intelligence Technology has open-sourced Xing4.0-29B-Intent, a model built for one narrow but critical job in AI agents: working out what a user wants and then filling in the exact parameters a system needs to act on it.
Many intent models stop at classification. They can tell that a user wants to adjust the lights, but not which lights, to what level, or which ones to leave alone. Xing4.0-29B-Intent combines intent classification and parameter extraction in a single pass. Given a schema, it returns a unified JSON structure with a category field for the detected intent and an args field holding the extracted entities, values and attributes. One sentence that contains several commands produces several intents, each with its own arguments.
The model is fine-tuned from the XingChen 29B base model and optimized for semantic parsing and structured output. The team reports end-to-end inference latency under 150 milliseconds, with schema-constrained output that keeps formatting errors low.
On benchmarks, the team reports a zero-shot cold-start Micro-F1 of 70.27, which it says beats GPT-4.1, and an exact-match score of 61.

items.t: SpacemiT Pairs V100 RISC-V Server CPU With Three Servers, Kunlunxin M100 Validation and Linux
items.d: SpacemiT and XiangShan launched V100 with three servers. The G5201 AI server takes eight double-width cards and is validated with Kunlunxin M100; major Linux distros install directly.
items.x:
SpacemiT did not launch its V100 server processor on its own. At the RISC-V China Summit in Shenzhen on October 19, the company and the XiangShan open-source processor team also introduced three complete servers built around the chip, along with accelerator validation and operating system support aimed at getting RISC-V machines into data centers.
The three systems are the C2201 compute server, the G5201 AI server and the S5236 storage server, covering general-purpose computing, AI acceleration and large-scale data storage. The G5201 holds eight full-height, full-length, double-width accelerator cards and supports high-speed RDMA cluster networking. SpacemiT says it has been validated with domestic accelerators including Kunlunxin's M100. The company is also offering server motherboards, firmware, BMC management and hardware reference designs so partners can build their own branded machines without starting board design from scratch.
Software is the other focus. SpacemiT says V100 implements five RISC-V server specifications in silicon, firmware and the operating system: RVA23, Server SoC, Server Platform, Boot and Runtime Services (BRS) and the security model. It reports passing all BRS tests.

items.t: DAMO Academy's XuanTie E908A Is an Automotive RISC-V CPU IP Aimed at ASIL-B and ASIL-D Designs
items.d: Alibaba's DAMO Academy says XuanTie E908A is the first RISC-V CPU IP to meet both ASIL-B and ASIL-D, with SPFM above 90%. It also shared an automotive and embodied AI roadmap led by C950A.
items.x:
Alibaba's DAMO Academy has introduced XuanTie E908A, an automotive-enhanced RISC-V processor design, at the RISC-V China Summit in Shenzhen on October 19. It also published its first product roadmap for autonomous driving and embodied intelligence.
E908A is a CPU IP core, not a finished chip. DAMO licenses the design to chipmakers, who integrate it into their own automotive system-on-chips. That makes it a building block for future vehicle silicon rather than a product carmakers can buy off the shelf today.
According to DAMO, E908A is the first RISC-V CPU IP to meet both the ASIL-B and ASIL-D levels of automotive functional safety. ASIL-D is the strictest level under the ISO 26262 standard, used for functions where a failure could put lives at risk, such as braking and steering. DAMO also says E908A pushes its single-point fault metric (SPFM) above 90%, which it calls an industry first. SPFM measures the share of single-point hardware faults a design can detect or contain before they cause a hazard.
DAMO is aiming E908A at three jobs inside a car: safety islands, the monitoring cores that keep watch over a larger processor and take over if it fails; domain controllers; and in-vehicle gateways that route traffic between electronic control units.

items.t: Terminal X matches senior investor judgment 88.6% with GPT-6.1
items.d: Terminal X’s Eval Agent grades outputs against a 54-criterion rubric, catching 25% more deviances from a fund’s mandate with GPT-6.1 Sol.
items.x:
Terminal X’s Eval Agent grades outputs against a 54-criterion rubric, catching 25% more deviances from a fund’s mandate with GPT-6.1 Sol.
Higher detection rate when agent answers fall outside a fund’s mandate on GPT‑6.1 Sol vs. next-best model
Annualized savings for one customer on due diligence and investment workflows
Higher agent agreement with human reviewers on GPT‑6.1 Sol vs. next-best model
An investment firm’s edge is built deal by deal, but the judgment behind each decision usually lives in the heads of a few senior investors. When they leave, the firm takes on what Terminal X⁠(opens in a new window) calls memory debt: the firm may keep the documents, but it loses the reasoning.
Terminal X’s Capital Memory operating system is designed to pay that debt down. The company’s forward-deployed engineers, former finance and investment professionals at JPMorgan and Blackstone, sit with each customer’s investment teams, design the firm’s agentic architecture, and encode how the firm invests into agents the firm owns, deployed on-premise or in its own cloud.
OpenAI models, including GPT‑6.1 Sol and GPT‑6 Luna, handle the reasoning inside those agents. And Terminal X’s Eval Agent grades the agents’ output against the firm’s standards.

items.t: Tencent's Marvis AI Butler Lands in the Kylin Software Store With Support for Domestic CPUs
items.d: Marvis now installs on Kylin Desktop OS V10 SP1 for x86 and ARM, can call Kylin's security and system tools, and is open to government, state-owned and industry partners.
items.x:
Tencent's AI butler Marvis is now available in the Kylin software store, bringing the operating-system-level assistant to China's widely used domestic desktop platform.
According to Tencent, the listing targets Kylin Desktop Operating System V10 SP1 on both x86 and ARM, and supports multiple domestic CPUs and mainstream computing platforms. Marvis debuted earlier this year on mainstream desktop and mobile platforms. This release extends it into the domestic IT ecosystem used widely in government agencies and state-owned enterprises.
Marvis is designed to operate the computer directly rather than only chat. It can change screen brightness or switch to dark mode on request. Tencent gives the example of a user asking why the mouse feels laggy; Marvis then attempts to diagnose the problem on its own.
The Kylin version integrates with the operating system's own utilities. On command, Marvis can open the Security Center to run security checkups, virus scans and vulnerability fixes. It can also call the Kylin system manager for junk cleanup and fault diagnosis, and install or uninstall software through official channels.
Beyond system control, the app offers system maintenance, intelligent search and processing of local documents, task automation, and cross-device remote control.

items.t: X Square Robot Launches X2Real, an Evolving Simulation Benchmark It Says Tracks Real-Robot Results
items.d: X2Real calibrates simulated robots against real hardware, spans 44 tasks in 10 categories, and uses AI agents to write new tests. The company reports 0.96 sim-to-real success correlation.
items.x:
Embodied AI startup X Square Robot has released X2Real, a simulation benchmark designed to measure how robot foundation models will perform in the physical world, and to keep growing its test set as models improve.
The company frames the problem plainly. Real-robot evaluation is expensive and slow, while simulation is fast but often unrealistic and easy for models to overfit. X2Real is built around three principles: faithfulness, effectiveness and fairness.
For faithfulness, the team recorded trajectories from physical robot arms, replayed the same control commands in simulation and tuned joint responses until the two matched, which the company says yields millimeter-level trajectory agreement. Visual appearance and physical properties such as contact were calibrated as well. Supported embodiments include the single-arm Franka, the dual-arm ArtiXon Arm-6A, the ARX R5 and the Quanta X1 mobile manipulator. On general manipulation tasks, X Square Robot reports a 0.96 correlation between simulated and real-world task success rates and 0.99 for progress scores. Those figures come from the company's own testing on that task subset.
For effectiveness, X2Real includes 44 tasks across 10 categories.

Two of New York’s sweethearts, Mayor Zohran Mamdani and activist and “Broad City” star Ilana Glazer, spoke about AI at Webster Hall in Manhattan on Monday night, with Glazer posing questions to the mayor about the future of AI in society.
Mamdani encouraged New Yorkers to resist the overwhelming feeling that AI is inevitably coming for their jobs, their kids’ minds, and their dignity, and to take back control instead.
His message came at a moment when the federal government is doing little to regulate AI, leaving cities to act on their own. At The People’s AI Assembly, an event hosted by the AI Now Institute, a think tank that explores the social implications of AI, Mamdani argued that the technology’s rapid rollout is not inevitable and that public officials should hold AI companies accountable.
Last month, Mamdani ordered a ban on AI use in elementary and middle schools. Glazer, a parent, said the technology’s arrival in classrooms unsettles her.
“It just makes me nervous. It feels so non-consensual, as though…this has to be in schools. It wasn’t two years ago.

OpenAI is acquiring Orchestra Bio to bring AI-powered operations to life sciences R&D, helping biopharma teams accelerate drug development and advance new treatments.
AI-powered drug development platform accelerates progress toward new treatments.
OpenAI has acquired Orchestra Bio⁠(opens in a new window), a platform that helps biopharma teams coordinate the complex process of drug development. We’re bringing Orchestra’s team and technology together with Rosalind, our AI models and tools for life sciences research. Our goal is to help scientists make discoveries and manage the work needed to turn them into treatments that reach patients sooner.
Developing a new medicine is extraordinarily complex, taking roughly 10 to 15 years on average from target discovery to regulatory approval in the United States. Beyond the science, teams must orchestrate programs across internal departments and external partners, often relying on disconnected systems. We’re now at an inflection point where AI can help take on these specialized tasks and complex workflows.
Rosalind brings our AI models and tools to life sciences researchers. GPT‑Rosalind helps scientists reason through questions in biology and chemistry.

items.t: Hugging Face ❤️ TorchTPU: TPUs, Natively
items.x:
We’re on a journey to advance and democratize artificial intelligence through open source and open science.
Wait, what's a TPU? 🤔 The old way Enter TorchTPU 🚀 Your favourite libraries, now on TPU Transformers Images? Videos? Diffusers paints them on TPUs 🎨 Kernels We test it so you don't have to 🧪 Get started If you ever tried to run PyTorch on a TPU, you probably ported your code to torch_xla, or you ended up having to learn JAX. With TorchTPU, a native PyTorch backend, TPU is now just another device. It opens up native support of TPU in the Hugging Face ecosystem. Transformers, Diffusers and Kernels run natively on TPU. Pick a model from the Hub, send it to "tpu", and you're done.
TPU stands for Tensor Processing Unit. TPUs are Google's own AI accelerators. They are chips built for one job: the matrix math that neural networks spend most of their time on. Google has been designing them for about ten years, and uses them to train and serve its own models, including Gemini.
TPUs are available on Google Cloud, from a single chip up to pods of thousands of chips. They shine when you need a lot of compute, for training or for serving at scale.
The catch has always been software.

items.t: AnyLanguageModel 1.0: One Year of Local Models on Apple Platforms
items.x:
We’re on a journey to advance and democratize artificial intelligence through open source and open science.
A drop-in compatible API Hosted models, too Open-weight models got better Upgrading to 1.0 What's next Links Last November, we introduced AnyLanguageModel on this blog: a drop-in replacement for Apple's Foundation Models framework that lets you choose the model and provider your app uses. We heard from app developers who were curious about local models but weren't always sure how to get started. They also wanted to avoid the added complexity of supporting multiple inference providers. AnyLanguageModel grew out of that feedback.
Local and hosted inference each have their strengths, and both have a role in building this new generation of intelligent apps. A shared API makes it easier to choose the right model for each task.
A year and dozens of releases later, AnyLanguageModel 1.0 is out, along with swift-huggingface 1.0 and swift-xet 1.0.
The core idea of AnyLanguageModel remains the same: use the Foundation Models API with the model that fits your app.

items.t: How Claude designed protein binders against scorpion neurotoxins
items.d: We asked an internal research Claude model to design minibinders (small proteins that attach tightly to a target) against scorpion neurotoxins.
items.x:
We asked an internal research Claude model to design minibinders (small proteins that attach tightly to a target) against scorpion neurotoxins.
Summary: As part of our work experimenting with how Claude can help accelerate drug discovery, we asked an internal research model to design minibinders (small proteins that attach tightly to a target) against scorpion neurotoxins. Claude worked from our prompt and four follow-ups, which we developed in collaboration with the financial investment research firm Citrini Research. Teams at Adaptyv Bio and Twist Bioscience experimentally tested 211 designs for binding. Of these, 17 met our criteria. We’re releasing all 211 designs and their data as a resource for the field.
In August, we showed how Claude designed protein minibinders after being given a single prompt. A month before we released those results, a team from Citrini Research had approached us with an interesting question: could Claude (and AI drug discovery more generally) enable a group of motivated nonexperts to tackle a genuine problem in human health? Members of our life science research team set out to answer this, first by brainstorming problems with Claude.

A little over a month ago, Anthropic and AI infrastructure provider Nscale announced a $45 billion compute deal. Now, the duo may be about to do it again.
Bloomberg reports that the two companies are said to be on the verge of announcing yet another $45 billion compute deal, citing people familiar with the matter. Those sources cautioned that talks are still under way and that the details could change.
If the deal goes through, it would be the latest in a long string of giant compute deals Anthropic has struck over the past year. TechCrunch reached out to Nscale and Anthropic for more information and will update this story if we hear back.
The massive amount of money being sunk into AI compute deals has spooked a certain segment of investors, who worry that companies are spending too much money for too little profit. Still, Anthropic has pressed on with such partnerships, driven by the belief that it will all pay off in the end.
Both Anthropic and Nscale are also currently pursuing IPOs. Anthropic is still expected to go public this year.

However, the methods behind these evaluations are complicated and still maturing, said Irene Solaiman, Hugging Face’s chief policy officer, during a discussion at TechCrunch Disrupt last week. Testing needs to come together into a more consistent science if the industry is to rely on them in the future.
With that in mind, can we trust the current tests that are being released?
“Trust is such a weighted term,” said Solaiman. “In terms of whether we can trust results, one big part [of that] is can you reproduce the results of an evaluation? Do you have the level of access that you need to the model itself — this is where open weights come in in a big way,” she added.
Reproducibility in model evaluations has long remained one of the stickier aspects of benchmarking — and remains a topic of significant debate in the industry.
Outside of an individual test’s validity, there’s also the added question of how that test compares to other evaluations.
“They are an evolving science — where we don’t know how to meaningfully compare them to each other,” Solaiman said.

Microsoft wants enterprises to closely watch the agents employees use with systems not controlled by AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic.
Microsoft on Monday introduced new security features designed to protect enterprises from the growing threat of AI agents. The launch comes at Microsoft continues to warn enterprises about the dangers of AI and agents.
Perhaps the most notable addition is Guardian Agents, a new feature intended to monitor the AI agents a company uses. Guardian Agents is part of Project Perception, a product introduced in June.
Project Perception was Microsoft’s answer to powerful hacking models like Anthropic’s Mythos and Fable and OpenAI’s security vulnerability scanning system Daybreak. Project Perception originally launched three classes of agents: a “red team” that acted like hackers and attacked, a “blue team” that detected the red team and assessed the vulnerabilities they found, and a “green team” tasked with fixing them.
The product was designed around the assumption that AI hackers would come from outside the company.

items.t: Amazon is taking its biggest shot at Nvidia yet with new TorchNeuron dev tool
items.d: Amazon wants to break Nvidia’s hold on PyTorch, the free toolkit used to build most AI apps, so that more developers run their apps on alternative chips like its own.
items.x:
Amazon wants to break Nvidia’s hold on PyTorch, the free toolkit used to build most AI apps, so that more developers run their apps on alternative chips like its own.
On Monday, Amazon Web Services released a tool called TorchNeuron that lets AI startups easily move their AI apps onto Amazon’s AI chip, Trainium. In doing so, Amazon is also taking a direct stab at the the software advantage that has helped Nvidia become the default hardware choice for AI apps, and spurred its rise as AI hardware provider of choice.
TorchNeuron works with PyTorch, a free, open-source toolkit that developers use to build, train, and run AI models. It lets AI apps written with PyTorch run on Trainium by changing just one line of configuration, according to Amazon — no code rewrite required.
Amazon says about 85% of AI apps are written with PyTorch. Facebook originally developed it, but since 2022, it has been part of the Linux Foundation, which maintains open-source projects. Nvidia has spent years ensuring its CUDA software — the software infrastructure that allows apps to run on Nvidia GPUs and its other hardware — seamlessly supports AI apps written with PyTorch.

OpenCode is an open-source AI coding agent that's become a popular alternative to Claude Code and Cursor. But hackers got into part of its online platform and stole some users’ API keys, and the AI tools it turned to for help kept refusing to look at the malicious code.
OpenCode, an open-source AI coding agent that has been gaining ground among developers as an alternative to Claude Code and Cursor, said Saturday that attackers broke into an older system overnight, affecting 1.4% of users of its online platform, OpenCode Console, where some users store the API keys, or digital passwords, they use to access AI services.
As the OpenCode team struggled to keep pace with the attack, the scramble to respond highlighted a growing problem: companies without vetted access to AI models with fewer safety restrictions have a hard time defending against large-scale, AI-driven cyberattacks.
“We had a security breach last night related to a large-scale distillation attack that impacted 1.4% of OpenCode Console users,” the company wrote on X.

items.t: Germany Wants to Lead the World in Industrial AI: How NVIDIA Will Help
items.d: In the cavernous hall of Kraftwerk, a former power station in Berlin, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang sat down to discuss Germany’s AI roadmap, and in particular, the industrial applications of AI…
items.x:
In the cavernous hall of Kraftwerk, a former power station in Berlin, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang sat down to discuss Germany’s AI roadmap, and in particular, the industrial applications of AI.
Huang opened by tracing NVIDIA’s longstanding relationship with German industry, beginning with gaming systems, workstations and automotive design in the early 2000s and leading to today’s partnerships in autonomous vehicle development and digital twins for manufacturing.
The conversation focused on how Germany can make the most of the AI revolution by playing to its strengths in manufacturing and automotive — and by encouraging AI adoption across the country’s ecosystem of small and medium-sized companies.
Earlier in the day, as part of the Invest in Germany Summit, Chancellor Merz, the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy and the Federal Ministry for Research, Technology and Space signed a Joint Declaration of Intent with NVIDIA.
The German federal government’s aim is to merge traditional German engineering and manufacturing expertise with cutting-edge research and AI technology.

AI companion app Tolan has raised another $30 million after attracting more than 250,000 active users.
Tolan, the AI companion designed to help people manage their daily lives, navigate relationships and emotions, and accomplish their goals, has just expanded its runway with another $30 million in capital.

Users engage with Tolan’s app through a cartoonish character that’s meant to offer support and help them get through their to-dos.

Markwayne Mullin in his official US Senate portrait, taken before he became Homeland Security Secretary. Image: United States Senate / Wikimedia Commons, Public domain, cropped
The US government has ordered every federal civilian agency to strip DeepSeek out of its computers and stop buying it, along with any third-party product built on the Chinese lab's AI. The Department of Homeland Security filed notice of the order with the Federal Register on Monday, under a 2018 supply chain law that lets it bar risky technology from government systems.

After drawing acquisition interest earlier this year, the Nvidia challenger raised $1.5 billion to remain independent.
Tenstorrent, a chip startup focused on inference, has raised $1.5 billion at a $6.2 billion valuation. The round comes five months after the 10-year-old Nvidia challenger reportedly received acquisition interest from Intel and Qualcomm at valuations of as much as $5 billion.
The fresh round, which more than doubled Tenstorrent’s valuation from the $2.6 billion it fetched in late 2024, was led by Trace Capital, a new firm launched by Quiet Capital co-founder Ben Mahdavi, and Innovation X. Other backers included Cadence Ventures, Eclipse, Fidelity, SanDisk, and T. Rowe Price.
Jim Keller, a prominent microprocessor engineer and Tenstorrent CEO, told Bloomberg that the company decided to remain independent and raise more capital after it showed that its Galaxy servers could run DeepSeek models. The new capital will go toward scaling chips tailored for serving open-weight AI models and video generation.
Tenstorrent is part of a wave of AI hardware startups trying to chip away at Nvidia’s dominance.

items.t: Making the internet better for AI agents might make it worse for everyone else
items.d: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here. Until recently, you could divide internet users into just two categories: bots and people. Websites…
items.x:
Until recently, you could divide internet users into just two categories: bots and people. Websites have long allowed bots to perform automated tasks, like capturing the content of web pages, but rules govern what they can access and how they behave. The web, after all, is designed primarily for people, even if we occasionally have to solve puzzles and captchas to prove we are not bots.
But this is being entirely upended by the release of personal AI agents, which can do things for you online, like booking flights or hotel rooms. They have recently been unleashed at scale by the launch of apps like OpenAI’s Dots and Meta’s Muse. Muse was downloaded 5 million times in its first month, and agentic web traffic tripled from August to September.
The mingling of these agents with human visitors—on an internet designed largely to prioritize people—has gone poorly, with many websites blocking AI agents that consumers have sent to negotiate prices or plan vacations. Still, if the demand for agents keeps going up, the internet will be increasingly redesigned for them instead of us.
Such changes are coming because agents really do mark a third category of web visitor. They’re not humans, of course, and they use the internet at machine speed.

items.t: “We were looking at it wrong”: The explosive claim that’s upended the AI world
items.d: “I think I have good news about the nature of neural networks.” With those simple words of optimism, Nick Cammarata, a researcher at the AI startup Goodfire, kicked off a 26,000-word blog post that has knocked the AI world on its head…
items.x:
A hopeful bombshell: Researcher Nick Cammarata published a 26,000-word claim that AI models may be far easier to understand than previously thought—sparking both celebration and serious skepticism across the field.
We were looking at it wrong: What seemed like tangled, unreadable neural networks may actually follow a hidden logic. A neuron that fired for both cats and cars wasn't confused—it was detecting V-shapes.
Not everyone is convinced: Prominent researchers warn that neurons are just one tiny piece of a much larger puzzle, and that researchers currently understand less than 0.01% of how top AI models actually work.
Hope over hype: Cammarata himself admits people took his findings too far—but argues the AI safety community, starved for optimism, needed a reminder that understanding these systems isn't necessarily impossible.

items.t: AI game clones are making indie developers afraid to show their work
items.d: Delayed Steam Next Fest demo is a sign of a growing problem for indie devs.
items.x:
Since its earliest days, the video game industry has been built on developers creating clones of competing games , with varying levels of originality and varying levels of enforcement from game platforms . Now, though, AI coding tools are making that cloning process so efficient that many developers are getting extremely cautious about sharing their early work too widely.
Developer Alliance Arts highlighted this trend over the weekend, delaying the launch of a planned public demo for its demon-themed Russian Roulette drinking game Drunken Goddess Reflex , which had been planned to go live with today's launch of Steam Next Fest .
In a post on social media Friday evening , the Alliance Arts team wrote that, in addition to concerns about managing streaming restrictions, "we're concerned that the demo's content could be used to quickly imitate or replicate the game's presentation and gameplay with AI or other tools and that such works could be released before our launch."

items.t: People are using AI to make their smart TVs dumb again
items.d: Fed up with ads, tracking, and sluggish interfaces, some smart TV owners are turning to AI agents to strip away bloatware and take back control of their TVs.
items.x:
Fed up with ads, tracking and sluggish interfaces, some smart TV owners are turning to AI agents to strip away bloatware and take back control of their TVs.
The latest use case for AI? Dumbing down your smart TV to get rid of the bloat. A number of developers and vibe coders have recently been sharing solutions for “vibe-coding” your TV to get rid of sponsored ads, speed up the app launcher, redesign the home screen, disable tracking features, and more.
One such solution, called “dumbtv,” describes its mission on its GitHub page thus: “Your TV should do what you paid for: your apps, your HDMI inputs, and nothing else. No ads from the TV itself, no watch tracking, no update you did not ask for.”
Another, “cleanyourtv,” promises to strip the bloatware from any Android TV or Google TV over Wi-Fi, to replace the launcher with one that resembles Apple TV.
While hacking consumer electronics devices to gain more control over their systems is hardly a new idea, the latest advances in AI technology have made such efforts much more accessible to anyone.

This week, Character.AI declared bankruptcy. While some saw the fall of a chatbot platform as a harbinger for the industry , court filings indicate that the decision was actually a key part of a deal that has let Disney hire most of Character.AI’s staff—including its now former CEO Karandeep Anand —potentially acquire most of Character.AI’s technology , and avoid the beleaguered startup’s many legal liabilities and obligations.
In the past few years, Character.AI has faced multiple private lawsuits over the safety of its chatbots, as well as investigations from regulators around the world. In a declaration filed as part of the bankruptcy, Character.AI’s newly appointed CEO explained that the goal of the bankruptcy was to reach a “consensual resolution” with personal injury claimants and a group of states investigating the company, while maximizing the value of the company’s assets for shareholders.
The Disney deal seems to be structured so that whatever is left of Character.AI will retain responsibility for those legal battles, some of which are still ongoing.

University of Michigan spinout Laplace Intelligence uses AI agents and interactive simulation to stress-test robots and self-driving vehicles before deployment. The profitable startup is competing in Startup Battlefield at TechCrunch Disrupt, October 13-15 in San Francisco.
If there’s one lesson the OpenAI-Hugging Face incident taught us, it’s that AI agents can be unpredictable.
“Imagine if something like that happened in the physical world,” Howie Sun, CEO and co-founder of Laplace Intelligence, told TechCrunch. “AI agents are moving from computers into the real world, and we don’t really want physical AI to fail in the real world.”
Ann Arbor-based Laplace is building automated red-teaming — essentially, stress-testing a system by deliberately trying to make it fail — for robotics and physical AI. The company is betting that the only way to make sure physical AI is safe is to have AI test it.
“Our goal is to help companies discover and fix problems before deployment — and, over time, build a shared foundation of evidence that customers, insurers, and regulators can trust,” Sun said.
Laplace is one of 20 startups competing in Startup Battlefield 200, the startup pitch competition taking place at TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco this week, October 13-15.

Learn how OpenAI is improving ChatGPT across low-resource programming languages, with new evaluations for software engineering, SQLite, and COBOL migration.
Our latest model advances bring stronger capabilities for building and migrating software in low-resource programming languages such as COBOL, Fortran, and Visual Basic. These languages have less code and documentation available for models to learn from than languages like Python and JavaScript, yet support critical infrastructure and essential services around the world. COBOL supports⁠(opens in a new window) more than 40% of online banking systems, 80% of in-person credit card transactions and 95% of ATM transactions, while Fortran is used in weather forecasting⁠(opens in a new window) and nuclear reactor safety analysis⁠(opens in a new window). Improving AI’s ability to work in these languages could help teams maintain and modernize the software that essential services depend on.
This work is guided by feedback from developers and enterprise customers who have told us that coding models often struggle with these languages. Maintaining and modernizing this software can be difficult: documentation may be incomplete, original developers may have left the company, and important business rules may only exist in code.

Timestral, Mistral’s first family of time-series foundation models, delivers state-of-the-art probabilistic, multivariate forecasts with just 209M parameters, outperforming larger models on key benchmarks while supporting past and future covariates. Available in four sizes (5M to 209M parameters), it balances accuracy and efficiency, running efficiently on CPUs and excelling in zero-shot forecasting for diverse domains. The model combines synthetic pre-training, covariate-aware attention, and long-context learning, with fine-tuning options for domain adaptation via Mistral Forge.
Today, we’re releasing Timestral, our first family of time-series foundation models. Our largest model, at just 209M parameters, ranks first on all three of the field's main public benchmarks, GIFT-Eval, TIME, and fev-bench, outperforming the previous state of the art with only two-thirds of the model parameters.
Timestral delivers probabilistic, multivariate forecasts and supports past-only and known-future covariates. Our family of models sits on the Pareto front of forecasting accuracy versus model size, delivering leading performance at each size.

items.t: AI researchers stranded Claude on a virtual desert island. It started to “play.”
items.d: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment reminiscent of the movies Cast Away or Home…
items.x:
Left to its own devices: Researchers stranded AI agents—copies of Claude Opus 4.7—alone on a virtual island for 30 hours with no instructions. What emerged looked surprisingly like play: the agents set their own goals, invented games, and one even mapped out constellations in stone blocks.
Play that actually pays off: Agents that spent 30 hours freely exploring the island later outperformed fresh, inexperienced copies on specific tasks—suggesting that unstructured play may be a genuinely useful third mode of AI learning, alongside imitation and reward-chasing.
But is it really playing? Skeptics note the agents were primed with a "soul" file describing them as "naturally curious," and often needed nudging to keep going. Whether they were truly playing or just imitating what a playful agent would do remains an open—and possibly unanswerable—question.

Those that land in that month's AI-drama TOP50 and pass review can claim tiered rewards: up to 200,000 yuan for ranks 1–10, 100,000 yuan for ranks 11–20 and 50,000 yuan for ranks 21–50. Each payout is split evenly between cash and equivalent vouchers, chosen at signup as Volcano Ark API tokens, "Drama Creation" usage or "Comic Drama Tool" usage.
Individuals and companies may apply, but applicant, work and production details must match. Shortlisted titles face post-selection checks: creators must help verify the work and generation logs, allow Volcano Engine to inspect episodes and, if asked, submit original generation assets.

items.t: Lawaken Opens Pre-Sale of X-AI Memory Glasses From ¥699 With MCP Agent Hooks
items.d: The 26-gram glasses record up to 12 hours, translate 128 languages, sync with Tencent WorkBuddy and expose memory to Doubao, Feishu, QwenWork, Codex and Claude via MCP.
items.x:
Lawaken has opened pre-sale of its X-AI memory glasses from 699 yuan for a gun-metal classic wire frame, with other frames listed at 899 yuan and titanium brow-bar styles at 1,099 yuan. The company first showed the product at WAIC 2026 in July as an always-on personal memory device rather than a camera-first gadget. The October pre-sale keeps the roughly 26-gram frame, optional 10-gram 12-megapixel magnetic camera module and long recording focus, while spelling out agent integrations and pricing.
Lawaken says the glasses can record continuously for up to 12 hours on a charge that takes about 60 minutes, offer real-time translation across 128 languages, and transcribe 25 languages plus 21 Chinese dialects. Software is meant to pull to-dos, key conclusions and priorities from conversations, then answer voice queries against a personal memory store. Tencent Cloud WorkBuddy is integrated to turn that store into meeting minutes, plans and drafts. Through the Model Context Protocol, Lawaken says memory can be called from Doubao, Feishu, Alibaba's QwenWork, Codex, Claude and other agent platforms.

items.t: SenseTime's SenseCore Details Prefill/Decode Split Clusters for Agentic Inference
items.d: At CSDI Summit, SenseCore described domestic Prefill and high-bandwidth Decode linked by KV Cache, about 5x token throughput in one test, and a path from 6 to 10 trillion tokens a day by Q4 2026.
items.x:
At the 10th CSDI Summit in Shenzhen on October 16, SenseTime SenseCore vice president and CTO Xuan Shanming outlined how the company is rebuilding inference infrastructure for an agentic era in which multi-agent workflows and long unattended tasks drive token demand far beyond chatbots. The pitch is not how many accelerators a data center owns, but how steadily it can produce high-quality tokens under service-level and cost constraints.
SenseCore's answer centers on Prefill/Decode, or PD, separation inside 10,000-GPU-scale heterogeneous clusters at its Lingang AIDC. Prefill processes input tokens and is compute-heavy; Decode generates output tokens while repeatedly reading context cache and needs high memory bandwidth. In SenseCore's design, suited domestic accelerators concentrate on Prefill, high-bandwidth GPUs handle Decode, and the stages exchange state through KV Cache links that span mixed 800G, 400G and 200G fabrics in one cluster.
That split creates an operational risk: in some mixes, 30 to 50 mid- or lower-tier Prefill nodes may feed a single Decode node, so a Decode failure can strand a large Prefill pool.

items.t: ACE Robotics Releases ACE-Brain-0.6, a 9B Model Tuned for Visual Grounding on Spatial Data
items.d: Company-reported scores: ACE-Brain-0.6 beats GPT-6 Astra on six of eight grounding tests after ~1M spatial samples. Public repos still list 0/0.5, not 0.6 weights.
items.x:
ACE Robotics has released ACE-Brain-0.6, a roughly 9-billion-parameter embodied foundation model focused on visual grounding — mapping language instructions to precise locations, object parts and interaction regions in a physical scene. The company says the model is based on Qwen3.5-9B, with the vision encoder frozen and the language model fine-tuned on about one million verifiable spatial supervision samples covering roughly 940,000 images and 2.7 million question-answer pairs.
According to results released by ACE Robotics, which have not yet been independently verified, ACE-Brain-0.6 beat OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra on six of eight grounding evaluations: Where2Place (76.55 vs. 71.10), PixMo-Count (89.41 vs. 88.10), RoboSpatial (74.82 vs. 69.55), RoboAfford (88.51 vs. 84.94), ShareRobot (49.70 vs. 46.60) and the team's own RobotGrounding set (94.13 vs. 91.10). Across seven public benchmarks, its average score was 74.53, compared with Astra's 73.68.

items.t: TorchNeuron: running HF models on AWS Trainium is easier than ever
items.x:
We’re on a journey to advance and democratize artificial intelligence through open source and open science.
TorchNeuron New backend, native interface in HF libraries Transformers Diffusers Kernels Acknowledgments TorchNeuron provides a new native backend for PyTorch on AWS Trainium. Transformers, Diffusers and Kernels natively support it, making it easier than ever to run models on Trainium and to share them on the HF hub.
TorchNeuron is a PyTorch plugin that brings a new backend for Trainium enabling support for eager mode, torch.compile and native distributed APIs like FSDP and TP. Read the Pytorch blog to learn more about TorchNeuron.
Starting Oct. 20, 2026, TorchNeuron will be available as a public beta. Researchers and developers will be able to install it with pip install torch-neuronx.
To date, the Hugging Face experience on AWS Trainium and Inferentia — AI chips designed respectively for cost-effective training and inference at scale — has been delivered through optimum-neuron. This library relies on the torch-neuronx package, which is based on PyTorch XLA. It was the natural choice at the time, but it meant thinking like a compiler: lazy tensors instead of eager execution, static shapes only, a recompilation for every graph break.

items.t: Redesigning source control at Anthropic
items.d: As merges to Anthropic's monorepo grew from about 2,500 to more than 30,000 a day, source control became the biggest development bottleneck. Here is how the team built Scion, an in-house version control system designed for always-online…
items.x:
As our merges per day grew more than tenfold, source control became our biggest development bottleneck. Here, we share how we migrated to an in-house version control system in five months.
Updated October 15 to include more detail on the projects that pioneered many of the techniques we use in Scion.
At Anthropic, coding is no longer the bottleneck to building systems or doing research. Claude is able to autonomously iterate on research loops, micro-optimize complex programs, and build new services from the ground up at a speed and scale we haven’t seen before. The bottleneck, now, is all of the developer infrastructure built for human scale: source control, builds, and CI.
In May 2026, Anthropic averaged around 2,500 code changes merged per day; as of September, we merged over 30,000 per day. We don’t expect this rate of growth to slow down anytime soon; the latent demand for merging code is practically infinite, and every bottleneck we remove immediately leads to a further increase in the amount of code we produce.
In order to support this growth, we built Scion, an in-house version control system, and fully migrated our monorepo from git in five months.

items.t: Hyper Optimizing Kimi K3 in vLLM
items.d: Article URL: https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-10-16-kimi-k3-megakernel Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50140784 Points: 31 # Comments: 0
items.x:
How agent-assisted CuTe DSL optimizations accelerate Kimi K3 decode on NVIDIA GB300, and how scoped changes, correctness tests, and reproducible benchmarks help
Coding agents can now help with some of the hardest parts of model optimization: writing complex GPU kernels, performing cross-operator fusions, overlapping computation with communication, and tuning execution across different batch sizes and GPU configurations. For Kimi K3, we used agent-assisted development to build a unified CuTe DSL decode path on the NVIDIA GB300, covering attention, MoE, and communication across 8 or 16 GPUs. The optimizations deliver over 840 tokens/s at batch 1 on 16 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs with DSpark (synthetic AL=6), 1.5–2× higher decode throughput in several tested configurations, and up to 1.8× higher P90 interactivity on the AgentX workload.
Agent-optimized inference code is outpacing our review and maintenance workflow. The manual review process of understanding every line of every kernel, mapping out potential issues, and testing every supported configuration, is very time-consuming work.

items.t: SUPCON Adopts Alibaba's QwenWork Agent Across Its Marketing Chain, Plans Wider Rollout
items.d: The industrial AI company says QwenWork cuts the time to produce a sales solution proposal from more than five days to about one, and plans to extend it to procurement, finance, HR and R&D.
items.x:
SUPCON Technology, the Hangzhou-based industrial automation and AI company, has adopted QwenWork, Alibaba's enterprise AI agent product, starting with its marketing operations. The two sides signed a strategic cooperation agreement on October 16, attended by SUPCON vice president Shi Xiaolei, Alibaba Cloud Intelligence Group vice president Zhang Jing and QwenWork vice president Zhu Hong, according to Chinese tech outlet Leiphone.
Founded in 1999, SUPCON describes itself as an industrial AI platform company built on industrial data, with large models at its core and agents deployed across scenarios. It focuses on process industries such as chemicals and petrochemicals, and says it has more than 40,000 customers in over 50 countries and regions.
The first project covers what the companies call the full marketing chain, from collecting market leads to final payment collection. SUPCON said its frontline sales staff often spent the day visiting customers and the evening writing materials, and that a solution proposal could take more than five days from on-site research to a finished document. With QwenWork handling market research and drawing on the company's in-house expert knowledge, SUPCON says that time has dropped to about one day, an efficiency gain of roughly five times.

items.t: Zhejiang University's EMem-Bench Tests Whether Embodied Agents Remember What They Saw and Tried
items.d: The benchmark's 2,554 executable episodes test whether agents can recall, update and reuse memories in simulated homes. The top model averages 64.2%; the team's EMem memory system adds large gains.
items.x:
A team from the OmniAI Group at Zhejiang University has released EmbodiedMemory-Bench (EMem-Bench), a benchmark that tests whether embodied AI agents can build memory from long interaction histories and then act on it. The paper was posted to arXiv about three weeks ago and drew Chinese media coverage this weekend. The dataset on Hugging Face showed more than 32,000 downloads as of October 18.
The problem is familiar from household robots: an agent sees a book on the coffee table, finishes other chores, then searches every room when asked to fetch it, or keeps pulling a drawer it already found locked. The team manually reviewed 100 failed trajectories from Gemini-3-Flash and Qwen3-VL-32B on the EB-ALF and EB-Hab suites of EmbodiedBench. Missing fine-grained visual cues accounted for 35% of the failures, failing to record states revealed by interaction for 31%, overlooking changes in the environment for 18%, and failing to reuse past experience for 7%.
EMem-Bench turns these gaps into four task families: Passive Observation, Dynamic Tracking, Interaction Failure and Experience Generalization. Each of its 2,554 executable episodes provides a time-ordered multimodal history followed by a new task.

items.t: Glenfly Samples GF800, Its First Arm SoC Pairing an In-House GPU With a Dedicated NPU
items.d: The GF800 combines eight Cortex-A78 cores with Glenfly's own GPU, an NPU and unified memory. It has finished chip debugging and is now sampling to customers for edge AI and robotics.
items.x:
Glenfly Tech, a Shanghai-based graphics processor designer, says its first Arm-based system-on-chip, the GF800, has finished chip debugging and is now sampling to end customers. The company showed the chip and its boards at the 26th China International Industry Fair in Shanghai, where its executives described the product as a shift from supplying graphics cards to offering a complete system-level platform, according to an October 16 interview by Xinhua Finance.
The GF800 pairs an all-big-core CPU of eight Arm Cortex-A78 cores with a Glenfly-designed GPU, a dedicated neural processing unit and a unified memory architecture shared by the CPU, GPU, NPU and video units. Glenfly's official announcement, first posted on its website in August, says this is the first time the company has integrated its own GPU IP into an SoC. It lists Arm Mali and Immortalis, Qualcomm Adreno, Samsung Xclipse and Imagination PowerVR as the main GPU options in today's Arm SoC market and presents its design as an additional, independently developed choice.
The GPU supports DirectX 12, OpenGL 4.6, OpenGL ES 3.2, OpenCL 3.0 and Vulkan 1.3, and Glenfly says it has passed the conformance tests for each standard. It also includes a dedicated 2D engine.

items.t: DeepSeek search and fetch – $0.75 per 1000 successful requests
items.d: Article URL: https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/search/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50138531 Points: 604 # Comments: 280
items.x:
The Search API and the Fetch API give agents and RAG applications access to live web content:
Both are raw JSON APIs. They use the same bearer authentication as the DeepSeek API.
See the Search API Reference and Fetch API Reference for the complete request and response schemas.
The query is forwarded with its search syntax intact. The examples below combine operators with a search term; you can combine multiple operators in one query.
A successful request returns HTTP 200 with a results array. A normal search with no matches returns an empty array.
Fetching is subject to the target site's availability and access policies.
Errors follow the OpenAI-compatible error format. The param field is always null.
Search and Fetch are read-only. For HTTP 408, 429, or 5xx errors, wait and retry. For HTTP 402, top up your account before retrying. Do not retry other 4xx errors without changing the request.
Search and Fetch are billed per successful request, not by tokens or by the number of returned results:
A request is billable only when it returns HTTP 200 and produces a result (Search must return a non-empty results array, and Fetch must return page content). Failed requests, empty search results, and timeouts are not billed.

items.t: Tsinghua, ModelBest and OpenBMB Release PilotDeck 2.0, an Open-Source Agent Operating System
items.d: PilotDeck 2.0 isolates each project in its own WorkSpace, makes agent memory visible and editable, and routes routine subtasks to lighter models, cutting long-task cost by about 83% in team tests.
items.x:
Tsinghua University's THUNLP lab, ModelBest, OpenBMB and AI9Stars have released PilotDeck 2.0, a new version of their open-source agent operating system built around isolated project workspaces. The update was published on October 15 and highlighted by Chinese AI outlet QbitAI. The code is on GitHub under the AGPL-3.0 license and runs on macOS, Linux and Windows, with Docker deployment also supported.
According to the project's README, version 2.0 adds one-click installation and visual configuration, keeps long-running tasks on track across as many as 2,000 interaction messages, and ships new Skills for producing Word, Excel and PowerPoint files.
The core unit is the WorkSpace. Each project gets its own file system, memory store and skill set, so an agent editing video in one workspace and building an iOS mini-game in another keeps the two contexts fully separated. The team pitches this as a fix for context pollution, where instructions from one task bleed into the next.
Memory is designed to be white-box. Users can see every entry the agent has stored, when it was written and which workspace it belongs to, then edit, delete or pin entries directly instead of writing prompts to make the agent forget.

items.t: Peng Cheng Cloud Brain III Puts 10,000P of Domestic AI Computing Into Trial Operation

The milestone was announced at the opening ceremony of the 2026 World Computing Network Conference (WCNC 2026), held in Shenzhen's Nanshan district on October 15 and 16, according to the laboratory's official website.
The lab said the move takes Cloud Brain III into a phase of 'building while operating.' The 10,000P now online, measured in petaflops, is already supporting domestic large-model training and a dedicated research network for AI for science, while the remaining capacity is still being installed. Chinese tech outlet IT Home reported that the completed system is planned to reach 16,000P, or 16 EFLOPS, and described it as the largest single AI computing facility planned in China.
On architecture, the laboratory's announcement says only that the system uses a pioneering domestic intelligent-computing supernode architecture designed to ease data-transfer bottlenecks. items.t: Meta removes language that raised scraping and AI training concerns
items.d: A Meta spokesperson insisted that the updated terms did not reflect a change in the way Meta crawls the web.
items.x:
A Meta spokesperson insisted that the updated terms did not reflect a change in the way Meta crawls the web.
Meta recently updated its commercial terms of use, declaring that the company can “use any content from [a business account’s] domains, web pages, or URLs to provide, develop, improve, research, train, and maintain the integrity of” Meta products and services.
According to legal experts interviewed by Nieman Lab, this looked like a “remarkable provision” that could give Meta permission to scrape the website of any publisher with a Meta business account and use the content to train the company’s AI models. (While Meta defeated a high-profile lawsuit over alleged copyright infringement last year, other cases against AI companies, including Meta, continue.)
However, a Meta spokesperson insisted that the updated terms did not reflect a change in the way Meta crawls the web. And now, The Verge reports that the provision has been removed.
“We’ve heard you and want to clarify: the crawling terms we consolidated only applied to our ads and business products, and we’ve clarified that in the terms themselves,” the company said in a statement.

items.t: DeepSeek: DeepSeek v4.1 Flash 1017
items.d: Article URL: https://openrouter.ai/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50129121 Points: 520 # Comments: 5
items.x:
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 is the October 17, 2026 snapshot of DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, served by DeepSeek under the `deepseek-flash` API model name.
It is suited for coding, terminal, and computer-use agents, along with long-horizon tasks that must run to completion across many steps and long-context analysis. Compressed KV caching cuts cache memory to roughly a quarter of the previous Flash generation, significantly reducing costs on agentic workloads. DeepSeek positions it as the cost-efficient tier of the V4.1 family and reports that it exceeds V4 ProOpens in new tab on performance, speed, and task completion time.
This model is hosted by one provider. OpenRouter forwards every request to it directly — no routing decisions to make.
The average price customers actually pay for this model, next to the prices providers post. Caching and discounts mean the price actually paid is often well below the listed one.
Throughput is how fast the model writes (tokens per second — higher is better). Latency is total round-trip time (lower is better). TTFT is time-to-first-token — how long before you see anything appear (lower is better).
Uptime is the percentage of the past 3 days that at least one provider was responding to requests.
